headline: Govt decreases petrol price Rs3 per litre, keeps diesel rate unchanged
summary: Pakistan government reduced the price of petrol by Rs3 to Rs325 per litre and kept the diesel rate unchanged at Rs358 per litre.
content: Pakistan government reduced the price of petrol by Rs3 to Rs325 per litre and kept the diesel rate unchanged at Rs358 per litre. The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) announced the revised ex-depot prices in a notification issued on Tuesday, saying they were worked out under the petroleum products pricing mechanism approved by the federal government. The new prices are effective for Wednesday, November 18. On Monday, the governmentreduced the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2 per litre each, bringing petrol down to Rs328 per litre and HSD to Rs358 per litre. Oil prices edged higheron Tuesday as a projected supply surplus driven by recovering Middle East exports countered concerns about continued tanker attacks and expectations of falling US crude stockpiles. Brent crude futures were up 32 cents, or 0.4%, at $92.76 a barrel by 1204 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures rose 39 cents, or 0.5%, to $86.11. The Brent benchmark has fallen 21% this month while WTI has declined by 18%.

headline: Sri Lankan shares slip as financial stocks weigh
summary: Sri Lankan shares closedslightly lower on Tuesday, dragged by financial stocks.
content: Sri Lankan shares closedslightly lower on Tuesday, dragged by financial stocks. The CSE All-Share index settled 0.14% lower at 21,701.07 points. Commercial Bank of Ceylon and Carson Cumberbatch were the biggestdrags on the index, down 1.01% and 1.38%, respectively. Trading volume on the exchange rose to 117.3 million shares from 80.2 million shares in the previous session. The market turnover dipped to 3.73 billion Sri Lankan rupees ($11.21 million) from 10.48 billion rupees in the previous session, according to exchange data. Foreign investors were net buyers, purchasing stocks worth 1.1 billion rupees, while domestic investors were net sellers, offloading shares worth 3.72 billion rupees, the data showed.

headline: Gulf bourses close mixed as shipping security concerns linger
summary: Gulf equities endedmixed on Tuesday as investors weighed the implications of recent tanker attacks and renewed efforts to safeguard key shipping routes.
content: Gulf equities endedmixed on Tuesday as investors weighed the implications of recent tanker attacks and renewed efforts to safeguard key shipping routes. Iran’s navy said a fourth oil tanker caught fire within 24 hours after hitting a naval mine in a restricted zone east of the Strait of Hormuz, while Oman’s foreign ministry said on Tuesday that Oman and Iran had discussed protecting sea lanes and keeping global trade flowing as Hormuz shipping remains disrupted. Saudi Arabia’s benchmark index eased 0.1%, hit by a 1.4% fall in oil major Saudi Aramco, as the stock traded ex-dividend. Brent crude futures were up 32 cents, or 0.4%, at $92.76 a barrel by 1204 GMT, as expectations of a supply surplus, driven by recovering Middle East exports, overshadowed concerns about continued attacks on tankers in the region and broader geopolitical tensions. Meanwhile, Houthi fighters have taken parts of Yemen’s southern coast after Saudi-backed government forces withdrew to protect Aden, military sources said on Monday. Residents are worried the Houthi will advance on the city. Dubai’s main share index added 0.6%, helped by a 1.3% gain in blue-chip developer Emaar Properties . In Abu Dhabi, the index advanced 0.9%. Fresh security alerts and new shipping incidents in the region this morning kept investors cautious, even as diplomatic efforts continued. Softer oil prices, under pressure from expectations of a supply surplus as Gulf exports recover, added to the wariness around energy-linked stocks, said Daniel Takieddine, Co-founder and CEO of Sky Links Capital Group, The Qatari index lost 0.3%, with the Gulf’s biggest lender, Qatar National Bank , retreating 0.6%. Outside the Gulf, Egypt’s blue-chip index declined 1%, with Talaat Moustafa Group Holding losing 1.8%.

headline: Copper falls to lowest since July as tech weakness saps risk appetite
summary: LONDON:Copper pricesfell to their lowest in four and a half months on Tuesday as weakness in technology stocks fuelled concerns about AI-related investment, hurting risk appetite, while a stronger dollar and expectations of higher interest rates added further pressure.
content: LONDON:Copper pricesfell to their lowest in four and a half months on Tuesday as weakness in technology stocks fuelled concerns about AI-related investment, hurting risk appetite, while a stronger dollar and expectations of higher interest rates added further pressure. Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was down 0.3% at $13,211.50 a metric ton by 0955 GMT, after touching $13,144 earlier in the session, its lowest since July 1. Stocks in Asia were down after Washington said it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia, tightening controls as President Donald Trump headed to China for talks with President Xi Jinping. “The sell-off in AI-related shares has raised concerns around the demand outlook for copper, given the metal’s growing exposure to investment in power grids and data centres,” said ING commodities strategist Ewa Manthey. Signs of tight prompt supply still offered some support to copper, visible in an increase in the Yangshan copper premium, a gauge of China’s appetite for imported metal, and the LME cash copper contract’s premium over the benchmark. The US dollar scaled a fresh 19-month peak on Tuesday amid bets for more aggressive policy tightening by the US Federal Reserve. A stronger greenback makes dollar-priced metals more expensive for buyers using other currencies. LME aluminium fell 1.2% to $2,967, paring losses slightly after hitting a one-month low of $2,965. Meanwhile, the premium of the LME cash contract over the three-month contract hit $278 a ton, the highest since 1988, amid low stocks. “We expect this tightness to continue supporting prices in the near term,” Manthey said. “Further out, however, the supply picture looks less supportive as stronger production growth should gradually improve availability.” LME zinc lost 0.6% to $3,676, lead was steady at $1,875, nickel gained 0.6% to $15,945 and tin rose 0.5% to $46,285.

headline: Rupee registers gain against US dollar
summary: The Pakistani rupee continued its marginal gain against the US dollar in the inter-bank market on Tuesday.
content: The Pakistani rupee continued its marginal gain against the US dollar in the inter-bank market on Tuesday. The local unit closed the day at 276.56, a gain of Re0.01 against the greenback. On Monday, the rupee had closed at 276.57 against the dollar. Globally,the US dollar on Tuesday ​scaled a fresh 19-month peakagainst a basket of peers amid bets for more ‌aggressive policy tightening by the US Federal Reserve following hot inflation data and hawkish central bank rhetoric. The US currency extended a 10-month high versus its Australian counterpart as a global selloff in AI stocks weighed on market sentiment, hurting ​the risk-sensitive Aussie. A sharper-than-expected acceleration in US consumer inflation last week triggered a run of ​five straight days of gains for the US dollar index, which carried into a ⁠sixth day on Tuesday with it rising to 103.66, the highest since April 2, 2025, when ​President Donald Trump rolled out his tariffs. The index measures the dollar against six rivals, including the ​euro, sterling and the Japanese yen. Traders now view a Fed interest-rate hike at the next meeting in December as a certainty, and they also lay around 4% odds on a supersized half-point increase, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch tool. ​A day earlier, those bets on an oversized hike were at nearly 12%. A week earlier, ​there were 16% odds for no change to policy. Oil prices, a key indicator of currency parity, edged ​higher on Tuesday as a projected supply surplus driven by recovering Middle ‌East exports countered concerns about continued tanker attacks and expectations of falling US crude stockpiles. Brent crude futures were up 32 cents, or 0.4%, at $92.76 a barrel by 1204 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures ​rose 39 cents, or 0.5%, to $86.11. headline: Robust inflows, pullback in shorts lift Indian rupee to seven-month peak
summary: MUMBAI:The Indian rupeestrengthened to its strongest in seven months on Tuesday, propelled higher by robust momentum in foreign equity inflows alongside the cutting of bearish wagers on the South Asian currency.
content: MUMBAI:The Indian rupeestrengthened to its strongest in seven months on Tuesday, propelled higher by robust momentum in foreign equity inflows alongside the cutting of bearish wagers on the South Asian currency. The Indian rupee closed at 93.47 per dollar, up 0.5% from its previous close and after touching a high of 93.40 in afternoon trading. Indian equities outperformed Asian peers, which slid due to weakness in technology companies after the US stepped up efforts to curb China’s access to advanced AI chips. MSCI’s gauge of Asian stocks dropped 1.5%, equities in Europe were lower and futures pointed to a weak start on Wall Street. India’s benchmark Nifty 50 meanwhile, rose 0.4%. Foreign investors have poured money into local stocks over November so far with month-to-date flows tracking at a record $10 billion. The scale of inflows has boosted the rupee with the rally sparking an adjustment of trading positions. On Tuesday, three traders pointed to sizeable flows in the dollar-rupee non-deliverable forward market, likely linked to the unwinding of bearish rupee wagers. The flows pushed the rupee into a modest premium in the NDF market compared with the onshore forward market. The view on the rupee has “mostly turned neutral,” but the outlook depends on whether the sell-AI theme persists and oil prices hold sustainably below $100 per barrel, a trader at a Singapore based hedge fund said. Elsewhere, currency markets were subdued with the dollar index hovering near 19-month highs on bets on more aggressive policy tightening by the Federal Reserve following last week’s hot inflation data and hawkish central bank rhetoric. The focus is on earnings from chip giant Nvidia, whose results could set the tone for the AI trade. “We still think further weakness in tech/AI stocks should make additional greenback appreciation less sustainable as it drives more dovish Fed repricing,” ING said in a note.

headline: Indian equity benchmarks buck Asia weakness to close at highest since February
summary: India’s benchmark stock indexesclosed at their highest since late February on Tuesday, bucking weakness in Asian peers, as lower oil prices helped sustain a rally fuelled by record foreign inflows and resilient earnings.
content: India’s benchmark stock indexesclosed at their highest since late February on Tuesday, bucking weakness in Asian peers, as lower oil prices helped sustain a rally fuelled by record foreign inflows and resilient earnings. The Nifty 50 rose 0.38% to 25,387.40 and the Sensex gained 0.52% to 82,532.19. The indexes have gained about 10.1% and 10.8%, respectively, this month as foreign portfolio investor inflows surged to a record $9.53 billion. Other Asian markets followed Wall Street lower, weighed down by weakness in technology companies after the US stepped up efforts to curb China’s access to advanced AI chips and by caution ahead of Nvidia’s earnings. Eleven of the 16 major sectors advanced. The broader small-caps fell 0.2% and mid-caps added about 0.3%. Banks and private banks climbed 1.1% and 0.9% and notched record highs, while financials and state-owned lenders added 0.6% and 2%, respectively. A sustained recovery in FPI flows could favour large-caps, and with relative positioning in financials still below average, there is still room for the sectorto catch up, Jefferies analysts, led by Abhinav Sinha, said. Lower oil prices have also boosted domestic equities. Brent crude hovered around $93 a barrel on expectations of a supply surplus, driven by recovering Middle East exports. The Brent benchmark has fallen 22% this month, while WTI has declined by 18%. Oil marketing companies BPCL, HPCL and Indian Oil added 0.2%, 0.7% and 1.1%. Tyre makers MRF, JK Tyre and CEAT and paint makers, Asian Paints, Berger Paints and Kansai Nerolac added 0.3%-2.1%. Lower crude prices improve fuel marketing margins for OMCs, while easing input cost pressures for tyre makers and paint makers. Among individual stocks, Senco Gold jumped 3.5% after logging a 26% year-on-year growth in net sales value during the recent festive period. Brokerage stocks, including Billionbrains and Angel One pared gains on Tuesday after Reuters reported that India’s markets regulator is considering curbs on leveraged stock purchases amid record margin-funded trading.

headline: Head of China's Baidu warns of AI 'bubble' ahead of APEC talks
summary: SHENZHEN: Artificial intelligence adoption is not boosting profits for most companies, the head of Chinese technology giant Baidu said Tuesday, ahead of talks on the sensitive sector between the world’s top two economies.
content: SHENZHEN: Artificial intelligence adoption is not boosting profits for most companies, the head of Chinese technology giant Baidu said Tuesday, ahead of talks on the sensitive sector between the world’s top two economies. The health of the global AI investment boom is under question, as US chip titan Nvidia reports quarterly results later in the day – its first since former CEO Jensen Huang quit over a widening affair scandal. Robin Li, chief executive of Baidu, spoke during a panel discussion with business leaders in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, which this week hosts the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting. Asked about the current global landscape for the technology, Li called the situation “urgent”. The “penetration and expansion of AI into the application layer has arguably fallen short of expectations”, he said. “While there is intense competition at the foundational level, can we say that companies are seeing higher revenues or increased profits after adopting AI?” Li asked. “For most, the answer is no. If we fail to address this, the concern that AI might be a bubble could well become a reality,” he added. China’s Baidu revenue falls 4% as AI cloud growth fails to offset ad weakness Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to hold talks with US counterpart Donald Trump on Thursday during APEC. They are expected to discuss the risks posed by AI as calls grow for cooperation between the two tech powerhouses despite their fierce rivalry in the field. Baidu, sometimes called China’s Google, has made an aggressive push into AI in recent years. But its challenges have grown as a domestic consumer slump drags on cash flows generated by advertising. On Monday, the Beijing-based search engine provider posted a sixth straight drop in quarterly revenue, as Li acknowledged “headwinds in online marketing” despite “tangible results” in the company’s AI strategy. IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva told AFP in October that if investors lose confidence in future returns from AI investments, tanking stock market valuations, that could “lead to financial stability risks” worldwide. Market jitters over the AI boom have been heightened by Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO last week after admitting an affair, reportedly with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has increased scrutiny of how Chinese companies gain access to Nvidia’s most powerful chips to train and run AI systems, despite US export rules.

headline: Australia shares hit over one-week low as miners, banks drag
summary: Australian shares slipped in early trade on Tuesday, weighed down by heavyweight miners and financial stocks, while the central bank governor warned that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.
content: Australian shares slipped in early trade on Tuesday, weighed down by heavyweight miners and financial stocks, while the central bank governor warned that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside. The S&P/ASX 200 index fell 1% to 8,956 points as of 2315 GMT. It extended losses to a fourth straight session and hit a more than one-week low. Miners shed 2.6%, tracking multi-month lows in iron ore and copper prices as weak Chinese economic data and AI spending concerns dampened sentiment. Shares of both BHP and Rio Tinto declined over 2%. Financial stocks slipped nearly 1%, with National Australia Bank down 2%. Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock said, “What we feel at the moment is that the risks on inflation are still skewed on the upside,” at a panel discussion in Sydney. The central bankraised its cash rate to an 18-year high of 4.85% earlier this month, but hinted that its run of rate hikes was drawing to a close. Markets are pricing in a hold at its next meeting in early December. Energy stocks slipped 1.3% as crude prices dropped on signs of improving oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz and reinforced expectations of a global supply surplus. Shares of Woodside Energy declined 0.6% and Santos dropped 0.7%. Gold stocks dropped 1.7% as bullion hit its lowest level in over a year, pressured by the stronger dollar and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. Shares of both Northern Star Resources and Evolution Mining fell over 1%. New Zealand’s benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index fell 0.4% to 14,251.99 points. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand warned that global financial stability risks have continued to increase, raising the likelihood of a significant shock to the country, but said its financial system remains resilient.

headline: South Korean shares fall for fourth day on US tech drop
summary: SEOUL: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
content: SEOUL: Round-up of South Korean financial markets: South Korean sharesfell for a fourth consecutive session on Tuesday, as chipmakers extended losses on a slump in US tech stocks amid worries about the global AI investment boom. The benchmark KOSPI was down 74.24 points, or 1.46%, at 5,026.26 as of 0149 GMT, after falling more than 2% earlier in the session. A broad selloff dragged US stocks lower on Monday as fallout from Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO soured enthusiasm for AI stocks. “The 5,000 mark will be threatened due to worries about slower AI demand, but the index is expected to reverse sharp losses during the session after pricing in AI worries in the previous session,” said Han Ji-young, an analyst at Kiwoom Securities. Chipmaker Samsung Electronics fell 2.41%, while peer SK Hynix lost 0.63%. Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution slid 0.63%, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were down 1.88% and down 2.84%, respectively. Steelmaker POSCO Holdings shed 0.93%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics fell 0.21%.  Of the total 909 traded issues, 229 shares advanced, while 646 declined. Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 514.1 billion won ($384.88 million). The won was quoted at 1,341.8 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform, 0.39% lower than its previous close at 1,336.5. In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds lost 0.06 point to 103.42. The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield rose by 1.9 basis points to 3.758%, while the benchmark 10-year yield rose by 1.6 basis points to 3.998%.

headline: Japan's Nikkei slips as investors shun risk ahead of Nvidia earnings
summary: TOKYO:Japan’s Nikkei shareaverage slipped more than 1% on Tuesday, tracking a selloff on Wall Street, as investors remained on the sidelines ahead of Nvidia’s third-quarter earnings and Anthropic’s initial public offering.
content: TOKYO:Japan’s Nikkei shareaverage slipped more than 1% on Tuesday, tracking a selloff on Wall Street, as investors remained on the sidelines ahead of Nvidia’s third-quarter earnings and Anthropic’s initial public offering. The Nikkei 225 Index was down 1.1% at 58,998.39, as of 0149 GMT. The broader Topix slid 1.29% to 3,850.41. AI- and chip-related shares led declines, with Advantest falling 5.07%, Kioxia Holdings shedding 4.58% and SoftBank Group losing 4.1%. “Caution ahead of Nvidia’s earnings and Anthropic’s IPO is expected to keep investors from buying aggressively, adding to pressure on stocks,” Monex Securities analyst Yoshitaka Araya said in a report. US megacap and AI-linked stocks, including Nvidia, fell overnight on concerns over the outlook for the sector after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation last week. Enthusiasm for AI stocks also eased after the US government announced efforts to further tighten China’s access to advanced AI chips from firms such as Nvidia ahead of a high-stakes meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. In Tokyo, energy explorer stocks fell 3.7% as oil prices slipped on expectations of supply surplus, weighing on the sector, while lower US Treasury yields pushed banking shares down 3.07%. The market breadth was largely negative, with 62 advancers on the Nikkei 225 against 162 decliners and 1 unchanged. The largest losers by percentage in the index were Ibiden, down 5.44%, followed by Furukawa Electric , trading 5.35% lower, and Mitsui Kinzoku, which lost 4.43%. The largest percentage gainers in the index were Recruit Holdings, up 3.72%, followed by Credit Saison, trading 2.59% higher, and Yokogawa Electric Corporation , which gained 2.32%.

headline: Copper extends losses on AI worries, dollar strength
summary: Copper pricesextended losses on Tuesday as AI investment worries, a firmer US dollar and weak economic data from top consumer China continued to weigh on the market.
content: Copper pricesextended losses on Tuesday as AI investment worries, a firmer US dollar and weak economic data from top consumer China continued to weigh on the market. Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was down 0.2% to $13,225 a metric ton by 0205 GMT, after touching its lowest level since July 1 earlier in the session. The most-traded copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange fell 0.6% to 100,890 yuan ($15,139.10) a ton, its lowest level since June 25. The dollar scaled a fresh 19-month peak against a basket of peers amid bets for more aggressive policy tightening by the US Federal Reserve. A stronger dollar makes greenback-priced metals more expensive for buyers overseas. Copper fell as the ongoing selloff across the technology sector raised concerns about weaker demand, a trend exacerbated by worries about Chinese growth, Daniel Hynes, senior commodity strategist at ANZ, said. The red metal is widely used in the power and construction sectors. Asian shares stumbled, weighed down by weakness in technology companies after the US stepped up efforts to curb China’s access to advanced AI chips, escalating the race for technological dominance. Data on Monday showed fresh signs of sluggishness in China’s economy in October, as factory production slowed and consumption remained weak. Despite this, the Yangshan copper premium, a measure of China’s demand for imported metal, remained at record highs. LME aluminium was down 0.8% after hitting a one-month low in the previous session. Meanwhile, SHFE aluminum slipped 0.8% after scaling its lowest level since December 2025 on Monday. China’s aluminium production rose 1.8% in October from the same month a year earlier, official data showed, keeping the world’s biggest producer on track for record annual output of more than 46 million metric tons. Among other LME metals, zinc eased 0.5%, lead dipped 0.1%, nickel gained 0.3% and tin fell 0.1%. On the SHFE, zinc declined 0.4%, lead lost 0.8%, nickel dropped 0.7% and tin added 0.4%.

headline: Dubai's DXB passenger traffic down 28% in first nine months as conflict disrupts regional travel
summary: DUBAI:Dubai International Airport(DXB) welcomed 50.4 million passengers in the first nine months of 2026, down 28.1% compared to the same period a year earlier, its operator Dubai Airports said on Tuesday, as disruptions from the Middle East conflict affected regional travel.
content: DUBAI:Dubai International Airport(DXB) welcomed 50.4 million passengers in the first nine months of 2026, down 28.1% compared to the same period a year earlier, its operator Dubai Airports said on Tuesday, as disruptions from the Middle East conflict affected regional travel. The war has severely disrupted travel across the region this year, as several countries intermittently closed their airspace early in the conflict. Gulf carriers, among the world’s largest international airlines, have gradually restored operations, but recent attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis have clouded prospects for a full recovery. DXB, one of the busiest hubs for international travel, welcomed 18.8 million guests in the third quarter, a 22.1% drop from a year earlier. Dubai Airports expects passenger traffic at the airport to reach 70 million passengers this year, CEO Paul Griffiths said in a statement. Some airlines that had suspended flights to the region due to the war started to fly back to Dubai in recent months, includingBritish Airways, Dubai Airports said. “Direct and transfer traffic remained broadly balanced during the year, underlining DXB’s role both as a gateway to Dubai and a connecting point for global travel,” it said.

headline: Yuan steady despite firm dollar as PBOC strengthens fixing ahead of APEC
summary: HONG KONG:China’s yuanheld near a two-week high against the US dollar on Tuesday after the central bank set a stronger midpoint that helped offset renewed greenback strength ahead of an APEC summit this week.
content: HONG KONG:China’s yuanheld near a two-week high against the US dollar on Tuesday after the central bank set a stronger midpoint that helped offset renewed greenback strength ahead of an APEC summit this week. The yuan was 0.02% lower at 6.6652 to the dollar, hovering near its strongest level since November 3. The offshore yuan traded at 6.6655 yuan per dollar, down about 0.01% in Asian trade. Prior to the market opening, the People’s Bank of China set the midpoint rate at 6.7132 per dollar, its strongest since February 2, 2023, although weaker than a Reuters estimate. The spot yuan is allowed to trade 2% either side of the fixed midpoint each day. The strong fixing came as the US dollar found renewed support on expectations of more aggressive policy tightening by the Federal Reserve following hot inflation data and hawkish central bank rhetoric. It also came ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on November 18-19, where Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold a trilateral meeting and discuss global flashpoints, ranging from trade policy and the wars in Ukraine and Iran to nuclear weapons and artificial intelligence. “Such meetings typically signal a marginal improvement in sentiment and risk appetite,” analysts at Nanhua Futures said in a note. “The meeting itself does not necessarily guarantee economic or trade outcomes… But if specific arrangements regarding tariffs or economic and trade cooperation are announced after the meeting, the yuan and overall risk appetite would receive a meaningful boost,” they added. Elsewhere, the dollar index was steady at 103.53 after scaling a fresh 19-month peak against a basket of peers. Traders now view a Fed interest-rate hike at the next meeting in December as a certainty, and they also lay around 4% odds on a half-point increase, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch tool.

headline: Australian dollar hits 10-month low; kiwi hovers near 2009 crisis-era levels
summary: SYDNEY: TheAustralian dollarweakened to a 10-month low on Tuesday as a selloff in global stocks battered risk appetite, while the kiwi hovered just above levels last seen during the global financial crisis in 2009.
content: SYDNEY: TheAustralian dollarweakened to a 10-month low on Tuesday as a selloff in global stocks battered risk appetite, while the kiwi hovered just above levels last seen during the global financial crisis in 2009. The Aussie hit a low of $0.6728 before bouncing 0.1% to $0.6743. The currency skidded 0.6% overnight for a fifth consecutive session of declines. “Near term, a test of the 0.6663 year-to-date low looks increasingly likely, particularly if US rates remain elevated and risk sentiment stays fragile,” said Rodrigo Catril, a senior FX strategist at the National Australia Bank. The kiwi dollar hit a new 19-month low of $0.5492, after falling 0.5% overnight. It is closing in on key support at $0.5485 and a break below that level could pave the way to levels not seen since 2009. Beyond the broader risk-off mood, the kiwi has also been pressured by lower interest rates than in Australia. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand has raised rates twice this year to 2.75%, well below Australia’s 4.85%, and shocked markets by pausing in a razor-thin vote last month. Data from RBNZ showed inflation expectations over the next two years nudged higher to 2.36% in the fourth quarter from 2.34%, though the increase was small and remained within the central bank’s 1% to 3% target band. Swaps now imply a 78% probability that the RBNZ will raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point to 3%, with a total of 85 basis points of tightening priced in by the end of next year. The Reserve Bank of Australia released the minutes of its latest policy meeting on Tuesday, where it delivered the fifth rate hike this year in a 6-3 split decision. Six members backed a rate hike, arguing financial conditions were not restrictive enough to tame inflation, while three feared the Australian economy was on the verge of a sharp downturn. “The message we take from the minutes is that there is a high degree of uncertainty about the future path for policy and the broader economic outlook,” said Adam Boyton, head of Australian economics at ANZ. “We continue to view the cash rate as having peaked at 4.85%. That said, a further tightening in monetary policy cannot be completely ruled out.”

headline: Indian bonds gain as oil slide eases rate hike concerns
summary: MUMBAI:Indian government bondsrose in early trade on Tuesday as plunging oil prices eased rate hike concerns sparked by elevated inflation readings.The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield was at 7.2813% as of 10 a.m. IST, down from 7.3169% on Monday.“Falling crude offers India’s bond market a timely cushion as it could ease pressure on inflation and the local currency, somewhat negating the fears of aggressive rate hikes next month,” a trader with a foreign bank said.Oil prices fell on Monday, with benchmark Brent crude dropping 3.5% as signs of recovering shipments through the Strait of Hormuz reinforced expectations of a global supply surplus in the coming months.The International Energy Agency said on Friday that the oil market could return to surplus in the fourth quarter as Middle Eastern exports recover faster than global demand, offering relief to major oil importers.For import-dependent India, cheaper crude is particularly significant, as lower oil prices can reduce pressure on thecurrent account deficit, support the rupee and soften inflation.The relief comes as markets had been increasingly positioned for another Reserve Bank of India rate increase in early December, with some even expecting a larger-sized move after India’s retail inflation accelerated to 6.09% in October, moving above the RBI’s 6% upper tolerance threshold for the first time in two years.Adding to concerns, US Treasury yields have jumped after stronger-than-expected October inflation data and hawkish Fed comments.Markets are reassessing the prospect of a larger rate hike on December 9, with CME FedWatch putting the odds at about 5%.

headline: Canada and China extend trade deals as Xi meets Carney ahead of APEC summit
summary: SHENZHEN: China will cut tariffs on Canadian exports including pork and seafood,Prime Minister Mark Carney’soffice said on Tuesday, as he hailed “greater predictability and stability” in China-Canada relations.Meeting withChinese President Xi Jinpingin the southern Chinese tech and manufacturing hub of Shenzhen ahead of theAsia-Pacific Economic Cooperation(APEC) summit, Carney said Canada was well ahead of schedule in its goal of boosting exports to China “by 50% by the end of this decade.”A major plank of Carney’s economic strategy is to reduce Canada’s heavy reliance on the United States, which has imposed hefty tariffs on many Canadian products.Xi and Carney agreed to extend and expand a preliminary arrangement to improve access to the Chinese market for Canada’s farmers and seafood harvesters, a statement from Carney’s office said.China will provide additional tariff relief for around C$400 million ($280 million) in Canadian exports, including frozen pork cuts and fish and seafood.In exchange, Canada has agreed to extend by two years existing remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminum products that are currently set to expire at the end of 2026, the statement said.Xi said that since the two countries agreed in January to advance the China-Canada strategic partnership, exchanges and cooperation across various fields have fully resumed.“Stronger communication and cooperation between China and Canada will benefit not only our two countries but also Asia-Pacific and the world,” Xi told Carney during their meeting.Tuesday’s talks marked the third meeting between Carney and Xi since Carney became prime minister; the two also met on the sidelines of last year’s APEC summit in South Korea.Chinese automakersBYD, Geely and Chery have taken steps to enter the Canadian market since Ottawa approved annual imports of 49,000 cars at a tariff rate of 6.1%.The quota is set to rise to 70,000 cars over five years.China also lowered tariffs on Canadian canola seed following Carney’s January visit, and recently extended tariff relief for Canadian canola meal, lobsters, crabs and peas for two more years.Shipments of Canadian crude oil to China have risen about 37% in 2026, according to a Reuters calculation based on LSEG data.Still, security analysts and human rights groups have warned that closer ties with Beijing could compromise Canadian security and values.Critics have pointed to the imprisonment of Hong Kong pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai, China’s secret execution of four Canadians last year and Canadian intelligence findings that Beijing interfered in at least two federal elections.China has said it has no interest in interfering in Canada’s internal affairs.

headline: China stocks flat as chip curbs lift local tech, hit internet giants
summary: HONG KONG:Chinese stocksstruggled to recover from multi-month lows on Tuesday as investors assessed the impact of tighter US restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips and awaited the APEC summit.China’s blue-chip CSI300 index was up 0.05% at the midday break after dipping to thelowest since July 2025.The Shanghai Composite index was nearly flat at 3,602.07 points, having slid as much as 1% earlier in the session to the lowest since August 2025.Tech shares helped lift the broader market, with the startup board ChiNext Composite index 0.7% higher and Shanghai’s tech-focused STAR50 index up 3.3%.The CSI Semiconductor Index rallied nearly 6% and the info tech sector added 2.6%, as investors bet the Trump administration’s further restriction on China’s access to advanced US AI chips could benefit local players.Shares in Chinese internet giants, on the other hand, slid on concerns that the limited access to advanced chips would hinder their AI ambitions. Alibaba fell nearly 5%, while Baidu shed nearly 7%.That dragged the broader Hong Kong market lower.The Hang Seng Index was down 0.8% at 23,571.61, and the Hang Seng Tech Index lost 0.5%.“We expect greater differentiation even within the same sector,” analysts at Morgan Stanley wrote in a note.Further tech restrictions against China will strengthen the policy and demand case for domestic self-sufficiency plays, while increasing risks for offshore names that rely on US-licensed hardware or offshore computing capacity, they added.Investors were also watching the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on November 18-19.Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold a trilateral meetingto discuss global flashpoints, ranging from trade policy and the wars in Ukraine and Iran to nuclear weapons and artificial intelligence.Elsewhere in Asia, markets followed Wall Street lower as US-China technology restrictions weighed on sentiment ahead of Nvidia’s earnings.

headline: Malaysian palm oil drops over 1%, snaps four-session rally
summary: KUALA LUMPUR:Malaysian palm oil futuresretreated more than 1% on Tuesday, snapping a four-session rally, as the contract tracked weakness in rival edible oils, although bargain buying helped curb some losses.The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 79 ringgit, or 1.74%, to 4,468 ringgit ($1,091.62) a metric ton by the midday break.The market came under heavy selling pressure due to broad-based weakness across the edible oil complex following a 3% overnight decline in crude oil prices, a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said.“The contract faced sustained selling pressure before bargain hunting emerged to pare losses,” the trader added.Oil prices fell as expectations of a supply surplus, fuelled by recovering Middle East exports, outweighed concerns over continued attacks on tankers in the region and broader geopolitical tensions.Weaker crude oil futures make palm a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.Dalian’s most-active soyoil contract fell 1.91%, while its palm oil contract shed 2.35%.Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were down 0.45%. Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.The ringgit, palm’s currency of trade, strengthened 0.15% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies.Cargo surveyors estimated that exports of Malaysian palm oil products for November 1-15 fell between 1% and 3.9% from a month earlier.Palm oil may retrace toward 4,441 ringgit per metric ton, which is close to the bottom of the wave d, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.

headline: Asia shares slide on tech weakness ahead of Nvidia earnings
summary: SINGAPORE:Asian shares followed Wall Street lower on Tuesday, weighed down by weakness ​in technology companies after the US stepped up efforts to curb China’s access to advanced AI chips, escalating the race for technological dominance.South Korea’s tech-heavy ‌KOSPI slid 2% shortly after the open, while Taiwan stocks fell 1.4%.Japan’s Nikkei eased 1% and MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan  extended early losses to last trade down 1.2%.Overnight, Washington said it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia.The new rule restricts shipments of advanced chips to data centres like those in Thailand and Malaysia that Chinese companies have used ​to access computing power to train AI models.The move came just days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of an affair with a woman who worked ​at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner that rents computing power at its data centers. It has come under scrutiny for ⁠possible illegal diversion of advanced AI chips to China.“This is a meaningful escalation because it extends restrictions from physically buying advanced chips to accessing their computing power remotely,” said Charu ​Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.“The impact could be significant for providers heavily reliant on Chinese customers training advanced AI models. They could face lower utilisation, weaker pricing and delays ​to expansion, while licensing uncertainty could make financing new projects harder.”Markets in China and Hong Kong slid, with the CSI300 blue-chip index down 0.5%, while the Shanghai Composite Index lost 0.65%.The Hang Seng Tech Index shed roughly 2%.A key moment for markets on Tuesday will be Nvidia’s earnings after the bell, with investors watching for signs of whether its debt-fuelled AI spending will continue into 2027 and how Huang’s departure ​could affect the company’s influence across the AI ecosystem.“With a roughly 7.8% implied move and a strong beat-and-raise already embedded, the bar looks increasingly tied to forward growth, AI ​ecosystem financing and export-control risk rather than the quarter alone,” said Torsten Sippel, UBS’s head of voice cash trading for the Americas.US stock futures edged higher in Asia, with Nasdaq futures up 0.35% ‌and S&P ⁠500 futures adding 0.13%.EUROSTOXX 50 futures , DAX futures and FTSE futures slid roughly 0.6% each.Concerns about the AI outlook continued to roil the metals market, with copper prices falling to their lowest levels in more than four months overnight. headline: US dollar hits 19-month peak on Fed hike bets
summary: TOKYO:The dollar on Tuesday ​scaled a fresh 19-month peakagainst a basket of peers amid bets for more ‌aggressive policy tightening by the US Federal Reserve following hot inflation data and hawkish central bank rhetoric.The US currency extended a 10-month high versus its Australian counterpart as a global selloff in AI stocks weighed on market sentiment, hurting ​the risk-sensitive Aussie.A sharper-than-expected acceleration in US consumer inflation last week triggered a run of ​five straight days of gains for the US dollar index , which carried into a ⁠sixth day on Tuesday with it rising to 103.66, the highest since April 2, 2025, when ​President Donald Trump rolled out his tariffs.The index measures the dollar against six rivals, including the ​euro, sterling and the Japanese yen.Traders now view a Fed interest-rate hike at the next meeting in December as a certainty, and they also lay around 4% odds on a supersized half-point increase, according to the CME Group’s FedWatch tool. ​A day earlier, those bets on an oversized hike were at nearly 12%. The petroleum levy circus
summary: Pakistan’s government appears to have discovered yet another way to discourage investment: persuade an industry to spend billions upgrading its facilities, then change the rules so that keeping them running becomes a loss-making proposition. And then have the audacity to thank the effected party, when it had literally dealt them a blow in the dark.The latest move to shift the burden of the petroleum levy onto refineries is more than another questionable pricing adjustment. It is a damaging signal about how Islamabad understands investment, risk and the sanctity of an agreement. Having spent considerable political capital presenting recently signed refinery agreements as a watershed moment for the country’s investment landscape, the government has now produced a rather spectacular demonstration of why investors might hesitate before taking those assurances seriously.The arithmetic is ugly. Petrol spreads have already slipped into negative territory. The proposed changes threaten to deepen losses on petrol to levels comparable to, if not worse than, those on furnace oil. Put the two together, and roughly two-thirds of refinery output could find itself in loss-making territory. Apparently, the government’s idea of industrial policy is to encourage investment in upgrading capacity while undermining the economics of operating it.One wonders what exactly the refinery agreements were supposed to achieve. Was the idea to attract fresh capital, modernise plants, improve product yields and reduce dependence on imported fuels? Or was it to secure investment commitments that could subsequently be treated as convenient places to park the fiscal costs of running the state? If the latter, the government deserves credit for efficiency. It has managed to turn an investment announcement into a cautionary tale before the ink has had time to dry.The timing makes the decision particularly difficult to defend. Refining is not a business that offers investors the luxury of predictable earnings. Crude prices fluctuate, product cracks swing, inventories generate gains one quarter and losses the next and global supply-demand dynamics can turn a profitable barrel into an unprofitable one with remarkable speed. Refiners understand market volatility; it comes with the territory. What they should not have to contend with is the possibility that their own government will suddenly rewrite the economics of their business to plug a hole in its revenue collection.There is a difference between accepting market risk and being handed policy risk by a government that has invited you to invest on the strength of a negotiated framework. The former is the cost of doing business. The latter is the cost of doing business in Pakistan.And this is hardly an industry emerging from a decade of extraordinary profitability. Over the past ten years, Pakistan’s refineries have averaged a return on equity of around 4 percent. Fertilizer companies, by comparison, have earned roughly 26 percent, E&P companies 18 percent, banks 16 percent and cement companies 14 percent.The numbers tell their own story. Refining has hardly been the most lucrative corner of corporate Pakistan. If the national interest now requires businesses to surrender earnings, why should a sector with one of the weakest long-run returns be among the first to receive the bill?And if this is indeed the new philosophy of redistributing corporate profits in the national interest, why stop at refineries? Fertilizer companies have earned substantially higher returns over the past decade. Surely, a few billion rupees from their profits could be requisitioned to make naan cheaper. After all, a loaf of bread is arguably far more essential to household nutrition than a liter of petrol. If refineries can be made to subsidize the petroleum levy, perhaps fertilizer companies can subsidize roti. One can only imagine the possibilities once corporate profitability becomes a public utility, available for appropriation whenever the state discovers a worthy cause.Did refineries make decent profits last quarter? Perhaps they did. Commodity businesses can have spectacular quarters. That is precisely why a single period’s earnings cannot be confused with sustainable profitability. A good quarter does not erase a decade of weak returns, compensate for future losses or make capital expenditure cheaper. Nor does it establish an obligation to return those earnings to the government through an unexpected change in the pricing mechanism.By that logic, every business enjoying a favorable quarter should brace itself for a visit from the fiscal authorities. Banks have made money. Cement manufacturers have made money. Fertilizer producers have made money. Some sectors have enjoyed substantially better returns for years. Is there a reason they should be spared? Perhaps their profits are somehow more sacred. Or perhaps it is simply easier to extract money from an industry whose pricing is already administered by the state.That brings us to the bigger problem. The petroleum levy has become an extraordinarily convenient fiscal instrument. Taxing petroleum consumption is easy, immediate and politically expedient compared with the far more arduous task of broadening the tax base, documenting the economy and bringing undertaxed segments into the net. When the tax machinery fails to develop depth, the temptation is to keep squeezing the channels that are already visible.But a levy is a tax instrument, not a magic wand. Its incidence does not disappear because the government decides to move it around the supply chain. Someone must ultimately bear the cost. If Islamabad wants to collect more from petroleum consumption, it should own that decision transparently. It should not quietly turn refinery margins into a fiscal shock absorber and pretend the industry can absorb the difference without consequence.There is something particularly perverse about asking a capital-intensive industry to finance the state’s revenue needs just as it is being asked to commit fresh capital. Refinery upgrades require substantial investment and long payback periods. Investors must have some confidence in future margins, policy stability and the regulatory treatment of their returns before committing funds that cannot be withdrawn at the first sign of trouble. If those assumptions can be overturned without warning, the risk premium rises, projects are delayed and capital seeks jurisdictions where the rules are less susceptible to administrative improvisation.No amount of official rhetoric about billions of dollars in prospective investment can compensate for that. Investors do not commit billions because a government describes an agreement as historic. They commit because expected returns justify the risk. A government that weakens those returns after asking investors to commit is damaging the credibility of the very framework on which its investment pitch rests.Pakistan can ill afford another self-inflicted wound in a sector already struggling to make a compelling case for modernization. The proposed upgrades are not charitable contributions to the national exchequer. They are commercial investments that must earn a return. If the state wants cleaner, more efficient and competitive refineries, it must create conditions in which those investments make economic sense.Perhaps the government’s approach is to demonstrate that no profit is too small to be appropriated and no investment agreement too solemn to be revisited. That would certainly send a clear signal to foreign investors. It just would not be the signal Islamabad appears to have intended.If the national interest requires every profitable business to subsidize the state whenever convenient, the government might consider extending this philosophy to the shipping industry. Freight rates have surged, and shipowners could be in line for an exceptional quarter. Why stop at refineries? Why not identify every sector enjoying a favourable turn in the cycle and ask it to surrender a portion of its earnings? There is always another industry, another balance sheet and another convenient explanation for why the burden should fall elsewhere.The absurdity is obvious. Exceptional earnings in a cyclical business are not a standing invitation for the state to rewrite the terms of profitability. Nor is the national interest served by making private investment a hostage to immediate revenue requirements.The answer is not to go easy on corporations for the sake of pleasing shareholders. It is to establish predictable rules, distribute the tax burden fairly and recognize that businesses need a reasonable prospect of earning returns if they are expected to invest. If the government believes the petroleum levy should be collected differently, it should make the case openly and provide a coherent policy framework. What it should not do is spring a surprise on an industry whose investment plans depend on the very margins it is now threatening.There is a fine line between wizardry and clownery. Wizardry makes the impossible look effortless; clownery makes the obvious look ridiculous. A government that promises a refinery investment renaissance while making the economics of refining materially worse may believe it is performing the former. To investors watching from the sidelines, it increasingly resembles the latter.And a circus, however entertaining the performance, is no place to invest billions.

headline: Barkat Frisian Agro Limited
summary: Barkat Frisian Agro Limited (formerly Barkat Frisian Pasteurized Egg Company) (PSX: BFAGRO) was incorporated in Pakistan as a private limited company in January 2017.The company started its commercial operations in 2019 and was converted into a public unlisted company in December 2024. After this, the company raised funds through the Initial Public Offer.The listing and trading of the company’s shares on the Pakistan Stock Exchange started in March 2025. BFAGRO is engaged in the business of poultry egg processing.Pattern of ShareholdingAs of June 30, 2026, BFAGRO has a total of 309.990 million shares outstanding which are held by 8141 shareholders. Associated companies, undertakings and related parties have the majority stake of 65.16 percent in the company. These include B&Z Enterprise (Private) Limited, Frisian Egg International B.V. and Barkat Steel (Private) Limited.Local general public accounts for 16.02 percent shares of the company while Directors, CEO, their spouse and minor children hold around 10.94 percent shares. About 3.57 percent of BFAGRO’s shares are held by Modarabas & Mutual Funds, 1.33 percent by Insurance & Takaful Companies, 1.29 percent by executives and 1.01 percent by Banks, DFIs and NBFIS. The remaining shares are held by other categories of shareholders.Historical Performance (2025-26)BFAGRO’s topline rode an upward trajectory over the period under consideration. Conversely, its bottomline picked up in 2025 and fell in 2026. The company’s margins which greatly improved in 2025 ticked down in 2026 except for the gross profit margin which stayed intact in 2025 and 2026. The detailed performance review of the period under consideration is given below.In 2025, BFAGRO recorded 19.42 percent year-on-year increase in its net sales which clocked in at Rs.7247 million. This was on the back of improved demand of the company’s products – both in the local and export markets.Local sales have the majority share in the overall sales mix of the company while its export market encompasses the Middle Eastern region with the KSA, Oman and the UAE topping the list. Sale from all the export destinations registered significant growth during the year.The company has an annual capacity to process 17000 tons of eggs. In 2025, the company recorded capacity utilization of 88.20 percent versus 74.59 percent recorded in the previous year.Enhanced capacity utilization as well operational efficiency achieved through various cost management measures enabled the company to record 39.75 percent improvement in its gross profit in 2025 with GP margin clocking in at 13.49 percent versus 11.53 percent recorded in 2024.Administrative expense mounted by 56.66 percent in 2025 mainly on account of higher payroll expense. This was the result of workforce expansion from 62 employees in 2024 to 114 employees in 2025. Increased freight and forwarding charges due to elevated sales volume coupled with higher advertising & promotion budget resulted in 64.11 percent spike in distribution expense in 2025. Other expense surged by 45.25 percent in 2025 due to higher provisioning done for WWF, WPPF and ECL.Other income improved by 103.22 percent in 2025 due to tremendous income on short-term investment and mark-up on liability waived by the associated company - Frisian Egg International B.V. During the year, the company raised funds through IPO which significantly strengthened its liquidity position. These funds were utilized to meet working capital requirements and also in other strategic avenues such as the acquisition of mutual funds to boost its other income.Exchange gain posted a phenomenal growth of 863.61 percent in 2025. This was mainly the result of realized foreign exchange gain due to conversion of loan into equity.BFAGRO recorded 50.53 percent enhancement in its operating profit in 2025 with OP margin clocking in at 11.28 percent versus 8.95 percent recorded in 2024. Finance cost dipped by 35.62 percent in 2025 due to a downtick in discount rate coupled with the widespread settlement of outstanding liabilities (through repayment and conversion into equity).Lesser outstanding debt coupled with improved cash position and increased equity due to issuance of shares through IPO and right offer resulted in a gearing ratio of 7.34 percent in 2025 versus 37.85 percent recorded in the previous year. No current tax expense was incurred in 2025 which was in accordance with the Clause (126E) of Part I of The second schedule of Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 on account of the company’s operations in the Special Economic Zone. This coupled with the effect of deferred tax resulted in the tax credit of Rs.3.02 million in 2025 versus tax expense of Rs.40.79 million recorded in 2024.BFAGRO posted net profit of Rs.741.687 million in 2025, up 95.30 percent year-on-year. This translated into EPS of Rs.3.68 in 2025 versus EPS of Rs.4.22 recorded in the previous year. NP margin picked up from 6.26 percent in 2024 to 10.23 percent in 2025.In 2026, BFAGRO’s net sales improved by 6.05 percent to clock in at Rs.7685.66 million. This largely came on the back of higher local sales. While export sales to the KSA greatly improved in 2026, other destinations such as the UAE, Oman and Bahrain posted muted demand. This was due to the ongoing tensions in the Middle East.During the year, the company commenced the commercial operations of its Faisalabad facility. This pushed up the company’s installed capacity from 17,000 tons in 2025 to 29,000 tons in 2026. The company recorded capacity utilization of 53.39 percent in 2026.Cost of sales ticked up in line with the topline growth which translated into 6.05 percent higher gross profit and a constant GP margin of 13.49 percent in 2026. Distribution expense surged by 18.80 percent in 2026 due to higher freight & forwarding charges incurred during the year. 63.26 percent spike in administrative expense in 2026 was the result of greater payroll expense, legal & professional charges and Ijarah rental charges incurred during the year.The company also expanded its workforce to 133 employees in 2026. Other expense dipped by 4.18 percent in 2026 due to lesser provisioning done for WWF, WPPF and ECL. Other expense was offset by 57.94 percent stronger other income recorded in 2026 which was primarily the result of fair value gain on biological assets.Dividend income and income on short-term investments also buttressed BFAGRO’s other income in 2026. Exchange gain deteriorated by 82 percent in 2026 due to high-base effect as the company realized exchange gain due to conversion of loan into equity in the previous year.All these factors translated into 6.75 percent diminution in operating profit in 2026 with OP margin falling down to 9.92 percent. Finance cost slid by 23 percent in 2026 due to lower average borrowing rates. This was despite increased outstanding borrowings at the end of the year which translated into a higher gearing ratio of 11.83 percent in 2026.While the company operates in the SEZ zone and is entitled to a 10-year tax holiday, it recorded a deferred tax expense of Rs.74.46 million in 2026 due to temporary differences between tax and accounting depreciation relating to fixed asset additions at the Faisalabad factory. Net profit dwindled by 15.43 percent to clock in at Rs.627.24 million in 2026. This translated into EPS of Rs.2.02 and NP margin of 8.16 percent in 2026.Recent Performance (1QFY27)During the first quarter of the ongoing fiscal year, BGAFRO registered a decent 21 percent growth in its net sales which clocked in at Rs.2274.11 million. This appears to be the result of improved sales volume, efficient sales mix and better pricing.Cost of sales surged by a lower magnitude of 15.56 percent in 1QCY27 likely supported by improved capacity utilization, stable raw material prices and the company’s efforts for backward integration and energy diversification. Gross profit enhanced by 59.69 percent in 1QFY27 with GP margin clocking in at 16.48 percent versus 12.50 percent in 1QFY26.Distribution and administrative expense spiked by a massive 135.61 percent and 57.72 percent respectively in 1QFY27 which appear to be the result of increased production and sales volume.Higher provisioning done for WWF, WPPF and ECL might have pushed up the other expense by 25.51 percent in 1QFY27. However, it was offset by 80.77 percent stronger other income recognized during the year which was most likely the consequence of fair value gain on biological assets and gain on disposal of fixed assets in 1QFY27.Exchange gain also strengthened by 330.61 percent in 1QFY27 further buttressing the company’s financial performance. All these factors translated into 47 percent enhancement in the company’s operating profit in 1QFY27 with OP margin clocking in at 11 percent versus 9.12 percent in 1QFY26.Finance cost mounted by 178.25 percent in 1QFY27 due to surge in short-term and long-term liabilities during the period. headline: CPI: the squeeze on households continues
summary: Food and fuel keep monthly price increases elevated. Softer core inflation offers some comfort, but households may be absorbing the shock through falling purchasing power.Pakistan’s headline inflation fell to 9.6 percent in October from 10.3 percent in September. That is welcome, but the monthly numbers offer little reassurance. Consumer prices rose by another 1.1 percent, the fourth consecutive monthly increase above 1 percent. Six of the past eight months have crossed that threshold.The annual rate Is easing while the cost of living keeps climbing. Households have good reason to pay more attention to the latter.Food and energy remain the main sources of pressure. Inflation averaged 10.1 percent in the first four months of FY27, against 4.8 percent a year earlier. The war-driven energy shock is keeping prices elevated, while domestic food supply problems are adding to the burden.There is some comfort in core inflation, which excludes food and energy. It eased to about 7.6 percent in October from 8.4 percent in September, suggesting that the broader transmission of higher energy costs remains contained. Even so, its four-month average of 8.3 percent remains above the 7.5 percent recorded a year earlier.October’s immediate pressure came from food. Non-perishable food prices rose by 2.6 percent during the month and were 9.6 percent higher than a year earlier. The monthly increase was sharper in rural areas, at 2.9 percent, against 2.3 percent in cities.Wheat and flour were prominent contributors. Wheat prices rose by about 9 percent in both urban and rural markets, while flour became roughly 7.5 percent dearer in cities and 9.4 percent dearer in rural areas. Chicken prices increased by about 17–19 percent, alongside increases in several pulses.The rural burden deserves attention. Average inflation over July–October stood at 10.6 percent in rural areas, against 9.7 percent in cities. October’s annual readings were lower, at 9.8 and 9.5 percent respectively. Rural households face higher headline inflation even though rural core inflation, at 7.1 percent, is below the urban reading of 7.8 percent.Energy remains the larger threat to the outlook. Transport prices were 28.6 percent higher than a year earlier, while housing and utilities rose by 11 percent. Urban motor fuel prices increased by 41.3 percent and electricity charges by 22.9 percent.LPG presents a particular winter risk. Urban prices were already about 69 percent higher than a year earlier in October. Further supply disruption would raise cooking costs for households and eateries just as seasonal demand strengthens.Its small weight in the CPI limits its direct contribution to headline inflation. That does not make the household burden small. Higher cooking costs can also feed into prepared-food prices, although the timing and extent of that transmission will depend on how much businesses can pass on.The distinction matters for core inflation too. Softer readings suggest that a broad second-round acceleration has yet to take hold. They do not, by themselves, establish the absence of wage pressure. Nor does contained pass-through necessarily mean households are coping well. Businesses may be absorbing costs through lower margins, while households cut other spending to pay for essentials.The Inflation outlook therefore remains uncomfortable. If food and energy pressures persist, the annual rate could return to around 10 percent in November and remain near double digits through the winter. Favourable base effects may subsequently bring the reported rate down. They will not reverse the price increases households have already absorbed.The State Bank has raised Its policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 percent. Its task is to prevent a persistent supply shock from spreading into expectations and broader price-setting. Further decisions will depend on energy prices, food supply and evidence of that transmission.But interest rates cannot repair wheat supply arrangements, secure LPG deliveries or remove power-sector inefficiencies. Those responsibilities sit with government.Fiscal constraints limit the room for petroleum levy relief. They do not excuse avoidable supply disruption or the continued transfer of energy-sector costs to consumers. Monetary policy can help contain inflation’s spread. Government must address the costs it controls.For households, a lower annual inflation number is welcome. Relief will require the monthly bills to stop rising so quickly.

headline: Karam Ceramics Limited: performance and outlook
summary: Karam Ceramics Limited was incorporated in Pakistan as a public limited company in 1979. The company is engaged in the manufacturing and sale of wall and floor tiles.Pattern of ShareholdingAs of June 30, 2025, KCL has a total of 14.55 million shares outstanding which are held by 306 shareholders. Local general public has the majority stake of 74.94 percent in the company followed by Company’s Directors, CEO and their children holding 24.81 percent shares. The remaining ownership is distributed among other categories of shareholders.Historical Performance (2021-26)KCL’s net sales dropped twice over the period under consideration i.e. 2022 and 2025. The company registered gross, operating and net profit only in 2021. In the remaining years under consideration, the company stayed in the negative zone.The detailed performance review of the period under consideration is given below.In 2021 KCL’s net sales improved by 21.53 percent year-on-year to clock in at Rs.1126.65 million. Stronger topline was the result of both higher sales volume as well as increase in the selling prices.Low-cost housing scheme initiated by the government coupled with the real-estate boom greatly strengthened the allied industries including ceramics. To make the most of the demand recovery, KCL produced 2.36 million sq. meters of tiles in 2021, up 31 percent year-on-year. This culminated into capacity utilization of 36 percent in 2021 versus 28 percent in the previous year.The company was able to pass on the effect of cost hike to its consumers, resulting in gross profit of Rs.35.74 million in 2021. This translated into GP margin of 3.17 percent in 2021. This was against the gross loss of Rs. 66.74 million registered in 2020.Selling and administrative expense continued to slide in 2021 due to lower vehicle running and maintenance charges, travelling expense, fee and subscription charges as well as advertising expense incurred in 2021. The company posted operating profit of Rs.80.51 million in 2021 which translated into OP margin of 7.15 percent. This was against the operating loss of Rs.13.76 million recorded in 2020.Despite monetary easing, finance cost surged by 8.64 percent in 2021 on account of increased borrowings. KCL posted net profit of Rs.41.63 million in 2021 with EPS of Rs.2.86 and NP margin of 3.70 percent. This was against the net loss of Rs.43.77 million and loss per share of Rs.3.01 posted in 2020.The topline growth of 2021 was followed by 27.39 percent slump in net sales in 2022. KCL’s net sales were recorded at Rs.818.08 million in 2022. The political and economic headwinds took toll on the infrastructure and construction activities in the country. Low investor confidence on account of deteriorating macroeconomic indicators as well as high discount rate resulted in depressed real-estate activity in the country.KCL’s production marched down by 41 percent year-on-year in 2022 to clock in at 1.392 million sq. meters. This translated into a thin capacity utilization of 21 percent in 2022. Cost of sales couldn’t shrink proportionately owing to escalated cost of raw materials and packaging material, high fuel and power charges as well as sharp depreciation of Pak Rupee.The company incurred gross loss of Rs. 198.04 million in 2022. Selling and administrative expense surged by 14.19 and 15.11 percent respectively in 2022 due to higher payroll expense, fee and subscription charges as well as legal and professional charges.Operating loss was recorded at Rs.199.89 million in 2022. KCL was able to squeeze its finance cost by 34.51 percent in 2022 despite higher discount rate due to increased borrowings from related parties for the retirement of external loan. KCL incurred net loss of Rs.251.76 million with loss per share of Rs.17.30 in 2022.KCL’s topline registered 19.44 percent year-on-year rise to clock in at Rs. 977.13 million in 2023. KCL’s production plummeted by 13 percent year-on-year in 2023 to clock in at 1.216 million sq. meters. This translated into capacity utilization of 19 percent in 2023, the lowest since 2018. This gives a hint that the inclined net sales were primarily the effect of upward revision in prices.The imposition of new taxes on property, dejected macroeconomic indicators, shrunken purchasing power of consumers and high discount rate kept the investors at bay from the real-estate sector. This radically shattered the performance of ceramics industry.Cost of sales mounted by 31.75 percent year-on-year in 2023 on account of massive depreciation of Pak Rupee, high commodity prices as well as hike in electricity tariff. Another reason for high cost of sales in 2023 was due to increased investment in repair and maintenance in order to boost plant efficiency and reduce cost.Gross loss amplified by 82.61 percent in 2023 to clock in at Rs.361.65 million. Selling expense rose exorbitantly by 131.35 percent in 2023 due to exceptionally high freight charges on account of elevated fuel charges. Conversely, administrative expense marched down by 10.48 percent in 2023 as the company replaced its permanent employees with the contractual ones which reduced its payroll expense.Directors’ remuneration also massively plunged in 2023. Other expense surged by 184.11 percent in 2023 due to massive exchange loss. Conversely, other income slipped by 92.17 percent in 2023 due to high base effect as the company earned gain on sales of its fixed assets in 2022.KCL’s operating loss magnified by 111 percent in 2023 to clock in at Rs.421.94 million. Finance cost ticked up by only 8.22 percent in 2023 despite high discount rate as the company considerably reduced its external borrowings. KCL’s gearing ratio drastically fell to 3 percent in 2023 from 64 percent in 2022. The company incurred net loss of Rs.474.96 million in 2023 which translated into loss per share of Rs.32.65.In 2024, KCL recorded year-on-year topline growth of 38 percent. This culminated into net sales of Rs.1348.47 million in 2024. During the year, the company’s production grew by 46 percent to clock in at 1.776 million square meters. This culminated into capacity utilization of 27 percent in 2024.During the year, the company introduced new brand “NOVA” with superior quality and design which was very well received by the market. 145 percent increase in the cost of gas over the year pushed up the cost of sales by 32 percent in 2024. This resulted in gross loss of Rs.418.78 percent in 2024, up 15.8 percent year-on-year.Selling expense inched up by 3.74 percent in 2024 due to higher freight as well as travelling & conveyance charges incurred during the year. Administrative expense ticked up by 3.2 percent in 2024 due to higher fee & subscription as well as utility expense incurred during the year. The company downsized its workforce from 369 employees in 2023 to 309 employees in 2024. This considerably reduced the payroll expense incurred during the year.Other expense tapered off by 84.28 percent in 2024 due to lower exchange loss as Pak Rupee greatly stabilized of-late. Other income slid by 3.52 percent in 2024 as unlike last year, the company didn’t record any gain on sale of its fixed assets in 2024. Operating loss surged by 11.95 percent in 2024 to clock in at Rs.472.37 million in 2024.Finance cost massively dropped by 97.56 percent in 2024 as the company sponsors extended interest fee loans to pay off external financing. This resulted in 9 percent downtick in net loss of KCL which stood at Rs.432.088 million in 2024. Loss per share stood at Rs.29.7 percent in 2024.In 2025, KCL recorded 56.68 percent thinner topline to the tune of Rs.584.21 million. This was on account of wavering investor confidence which kept them away from real-estate investment despite improvement observed in macroeconomic indicators.Market saturation and high competition also slashed the sales during the year. In line with weak demand, KCL’s production plunged by 75 percent to clock in at 0.442 million square meters. Capacity utilization fell to its lowest level of 7 percent in 2025. Cost of sales dropped by 36.85 percent in 2025 which resulted in gross loss of Rs.531.86 million, up 27 percent year-on-year.Higher gas price was the main culprit which drove up gross loss in 2025. Selling expense plummeted by 83 percent in 2025 due to thinner sales volume which pushed down freight charges, salaries of sales force and conveyance charges. Conversely, administrative expense surged by 45.94 percent in 2025 on account of higher payroll expense, repair & maintenance charges as well as legal & professional charges.KCL streamlined its contractual employees from 301 in 2024 to 293 in 2024. Other expense multiplied by a massive 2262.83 percent in 2025 due to provisioning done for refundable taxes. Conversely, other income deteriorated by 76.43 percent in 2025 due to lower profit recognized on saving deposits. KCL recorded operating loss of Rs.610.89 million in 2025, up 29.32 percent year-on-year.Finance cost escalated by 239.88 percent in 2025 despite lower discount rate. This primarily included finance cost on the amount released by the bank under guarantee issued in favor of Sui Southern Gas Company Limited. Net loss mounted by 68.54 percent in 2025 to clock in at Rs.728.226 million. This translated into loss per share of Rs.50.05 in 2025.Recent Performance (2026)In 2026, KCL’s net sales ticked up by 5.70 percent to clock in at Rs.617.48 million. The demand remained largely concentrated in renovation projects and selected public sector projects while private sector construction activity stayed muted in 2026.The company’s investment in the BMR of its machinery helped it reduce gas consumption, improve productivity and enhance product quality in line with the market standards. This resulted in 40.50 percent decline in cost of sales in 2026 with gross loss shrinking by 91.24 percent to clock in at Rs.46.61 million.Distribution expense mounted by 98.43 percent in 2026 likely due to slight demand recovery which might have pushed up freight charges as well as travelling & conveyance charges. Increased payroll expense, repair & maintenance charges as well as legal & professional charges appear to be the main culprits behind 21.38 percent spike in administrative expense during the year.Other income strengthened by 1169 percent in 2026 apparently due to gain recognized on the disposal of fixed assets as well as exchange gain recognized during the year.KCL recorded 85 percent thinner operating loss to the tune of Rs.91.62 million in 2026. Finance cost thinned down by 78.34 percent in 2026 due to lower average borrowing rate and KCL’s heavy reliance on interest-free, on-demand loan from a related party – Swat Ceramics.Lower finance cost in 2026 may also be justified as in 2025, the company’s finance cost massively increased due to the amount released by the bank under guarantee issued in favor of Sui Southern Gas Company Limited. Net loss shrank by 86.21 percent to clock in at Rs.100.457 million in 2026. This translated into loss per share of Rs.6.90 in 2026.Future OutlookWith wavering investor confidence, high excise duties and elevated property taxes, the demand for real-estate may not see any considerable recovery in the near to medium term. Moreover, escalated energy prices, inflated construction costs as well as geopolitical uncertainty will also pose risk to industry demand. Continued reliance on loans from the related parties flag liquidity concerns.On the positive front, the completion of BMR project has created room for margin improvement. The company also plans to expand its product portfolio to cater to changing customer preferences and diversify its sales mix.

This gives a hint that the inclined net sales were primarily the effect of upward revision in prices.The imposition of new taxes on property, dejected macroeconomic indicators, shrunken purchasing power of consumers and high discount rate kept the investors at bay from the real-estate sector. This radically shattered the performance of ceramics industry.Cost of sales mounted by 31.75 percent year-on-year in 2023 on account of massive depreciation of Pak Rupee, high commodity prices as well as hike in electricity tariff.
