Operating expense slumped by 6.90 percent in 2025 due to lower payroll expense as the company rationalized its workforce from 186 employees in 2024 to 162 employees in 2025.As against reversal booked in the previous year, PAKD recorded impairment loss on financial assets worth Rs.2.79 million in 2025. 10.48 percent uptick in other income in 2025 was the result of liabilities written back during the year. This included customer deposits and trade creditors written back. PAKD recorded 14.34 percent deterioration in its operating profit in 2025 with OP margin falling down to 13.73 percent.Finance cost went down by 57 percent in 2025 mainly due to lower exchange loss. Net profit dwindled by 20.43 percent to clock in at Rs.152.95 million. This translated into EPS of Rs.12.90 and NP margin of 8.24 percent in 2025.Recent Performance (9MFY26)During the first nine-month period of the ongoing fiscal year, PAKD’s net sales dropped by 16.51 percent to clock in at Rs.1066.291 million. This was due to decline recorded in revenue from data communication services, specialized projects and solar equipments sales. Conversely, revenue from telecom infrastructure services remained stable during the period under review.Cost of sales diminished by 9.86 percent in 9MFY26 which was much lower than the topline contraction. This was due to higher raw materials and fuel cost as well as supply chain disruptions in the wake of Middle East Crisis. This resulted in 37.16 percent contraction in gross profit in 9MFY26 with GP margin clocking in at 18.35 percent versus GP margin of 24.37 percent recorded in 9MFY25.Operating expense surged by 21 percent in 9MFY26 mainly on the back of elevated payroll expense, marketing & advertising expense as well as travelling & conveyance charges incurred during the period. Reversal of impairment booked on financial assets grew by 12.19 percent in 9MFY26.Robust income from short-term investments and bank deposits as well as gain recognized on the sale of fixed assets resulted in 26.51 percent stronger other income in 9MFY26. Operating profit contracted by 72.53 percent in 9MFY26 with OP margin sinking to 4.92 percent versus OP margin of 14.95 percent recorded in 9MFY25.Finance cost surged by 14 percent in 9MFY26 due to greater outstanding lease liabilities. PAKD recorded net profit of Rs.12.83 million in 9MFY26, down 88.35 percent year-on-year. This translated into EPS of Rs.1.08 in 9MFY26 versus EPS of Rs.9.29 posted in 9MFY25. NP margin nosedived from 8.63 percent in 9MFY25 to 1.20 percent in 9MFY26.Future OutlookPakistan demographic break-up shows that there is a large proportion of population under 30 years old who are eager to adopt new technologies and digital services. This may result in improved demand of mobile connectivity and high-speed internet.Besides, the growing trend of online education, remote work, entertainment, e-commerce, digital transformation across various sectors etc will also fuel the demand for PAKD’s services. The company has also recently ventured into the sale of solar equipments. This diversification of revenue streams will also prove to be rewarding for the company.PAKD is also actively pursuing renewable energy solutions, automation of internal processes and diversification of its ICT and data driven portfolio. These initiatives will support the company’s long-run growth plans.The key areas of growth for PAKD also include expansion of rural connectivity, improving government sector engagement and incorporation of cloud and cyber security offerings. Providing green energy solutions, expansion of fiber optic networks and leveraging emerging technologies such as AI and IoT are also potential opportunity areas for PAKD.

headline: SBP’s dollar-buying hunger
summary: The hallmark of SBP’s performance over the last four years has been its management of external accounts. SBP’s gross reserves have increased from a low of USD3 billion at the start of 2023 to USD21.5 billion as of now. Additionally, its forward liabilities have declined by almost $4 billion.Thus, the overall improvement stands at USD22.5 billion, while total external debt and liabilities have increased by $10.2 billion from January 2023 to June 2026 (forex reserves are up by USD15.3 billion during this period).Thus, the overall net increase of over USD9 billion is solely due to purchases from the interbank market. And that number must have grown further so far this fiscal year.The latest data show that in Jul-26, SBP bought USD863 million from the interbank market despite running a current account deficit of USD445 million. In the previous month (Jun-26), SBP bought $841 million despite a current account deficit of USD836 million. According to official data, from Jun-24 to Jul-26, SBP bought USD17.2 billion from the interbank market.As per the SBP Governor’s remarks at the post-monetary policy press conference, the central bank has bought USD30 billion from the interbank market over the last four years.Around USD12 billion was used for interest payments, while the rest has been used to build reserves. That is comforting news and has helped Pakistan move from the verge of default to a position where it is navigating the current oil crisis well. This, along with positive real interest rates and an improved fiscal position, has helped tame inflation.SBP is following a formula that keeps bank treasuries on their toes but works well for the country. For the past three years or so, SBP has implicitly not allowed banks to buy foreign currency from other banks. Whatever surplus they have at the end of the day must be surrendered to SBP, which then becomes part of the central bank’s dollar purchases.Thus, banks have to arrange dollars internally from exports and remittances to finance imports and other payments. They charge higher rates for imports while offering discounts on remittances. Earlier, the government was providing rebates on remittances, but now banks are bearing this expense out of their own pockets. On average, banks are offering a discount of Rs2–2.5 per dollar.That is helping remittances grow through formal banking channels. Banks are hungry for remittances, and they are competing not only with one another but also with the informal market, which is at a disadvantage following the crackdown a couple of years ago.Additionally, inflows are improving as the outflow of money from the market following the war appears to have stopped (or slowed down). Against this backdrop, SBP has increased its FY27 remittances target to USD45 billion.SBP means business, as it continues to buy dollars aggressively from the market even today. Import cover has improved from two weeks to over three months. But SBP demands more. It is hungry for dollars and is making life difficult for bank treasuries. The central bank has revised its reserves target upward to USD23 billion for December 2026 and USD25 billion for June 2027. SBP wants more.That is the right strategy. SBP should keep building reserves. However, it should not single-handedly squeeze the banks. Rather, it should also use currency pricing as a policy tool.The REER published by SBP stands at 109—its highest level since 2018. Whenever someone argues for allowing the currency to adjust, SBP starts talking about its buying spree (mentioned above). That is good, but not enough.Nonetheless, no one at SBP or in the government wants the PKR to depreciate. They fear that depreciation could create a negative feedback loop, potentially triggering dollarization. SBP is considering buying more dollars from the market and is planning to issue a dual-currency bond.Hence, the authorities want to keep the rupee stable while continuing to buy dollars.That may help build reserves, but it may not allow the economy to grow beyond 4 percent. To achieve higher growth while continuing to build reserves, SBP must allow the currency to adjust while managing market anxiety. But that may not happen anytime soon.

headline: Engro Polymer & Chemicals Limited: performance and outlook
summary: Engro Polymer & Chemicals Limited (PSX: EPCL) was incorporated in Pakistan in 1997. EPCL is a subsidiary of Engro Corporation which is a subsidiary of Dawood Hercules Corporation Limited. The company is engaged in the manufacturing, marketing and selling of Poly Vinyl Chloride (PVC), Caustic Soda, Vinyl Chloride Monomer (VCM) and related products.The company also has a captive power plant and water recycling plant in its integrated chemical complex. The surplus power produced by the company is also supplied to Engro Fertilizers Limited.Pattern of ShareholdingAs of December 31, 2025, EPCL has 908.92 million shares outstanding which are held by 32,939 shareholders. Associated companies, undertakings and associated companies have the majority stake of 77.35 percent in the company. Within this category, Engro Corporation Limited took the lead, followed by Mitsubishi Corporation.Local general public accounts for 15.21 percent of the company’s shares followed by Insurance companies holding 4.45 percent shares. The remaining shares are held by other categories of shareholders.Financial Performance (2019-2025)Over the period under consideration, EPCL’s topline posted year-on-year growth in 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2025. Its bottomline posted growth only in 2020 and 2021. EPCL registered net loss in 2025. The company’s margins which dwindled in 2019 posted significant growth for the subsequent two years. This was followed by a drastic fall in margins since 2022. EPCL’s margins hit their lowest ebb in 2025 (see the graph of profitability ratios).The detailed performance review of the period under consideration is given below.In 2019, EPCL’s topline posted year-on-year uptick of 7.27 percent to clock in at Rs37,836.63 million. The paltry topline growth was due to a slowdown in the PVC market owing to deteriorated construction activities in the country and the dumping of PVC from other sources.Chlor Alkali market also declined during the year owing to CNIC requirement, imposition of sales tax on local sales and also because of gas curtailment… During the year, the sales volume of PVC and caustic soda dipped by 6 percent and 4 percent respectively to clock in at 191 KT and 83 KT.In 2019, caustic flake facility also came online and registered sales volume of 1KT particularly in the export market. Cost of sales grew by 7.47 percent in 2019 due to inflation, Pak Rupee depreciation and higher gas prices.However, the company’s ability to venture into a high margin export market and implementation of cost control measures resulted in 6.54 percent improvement in gross profit in 2019 with GP margin clocking in at 21.42 percent versus GP margin of 21.57 percent recorded in the previous year.Distribution expense inched up by 1.78 percent in 2019 due to higher salaries of sales force coupled with increased travelling, conveyance and training charges incurred during the year.Administrative expense inched down by 1 percent in 2019 due to lower payroll expense despite workforce expansion from 455 employees in 2018 to 508 employees in 2019. Other expense mounted by 49.94 percent in 2019 due to higher exchange loss. Other income dipped by 25.54 percent in 2019 mainly because of high-base effect as the company recorded insurance income recognized in the previous year on account of business interruption.EPCL recorded 3.34 percent decline in its operating profit in 2019 with OP margin clocking in at 18 percent versus OP margin of 20 percent recorded in the previous year. Finance cost surged by 196.22 percent in 2019 on the back of high discount rate and increase in the utilization of borrowing lines.Net profit tumbled by 25 percent to clock in at Rs.3696.06 million in 2019 with EPS of Rs.4.07 versus EPS of Rs.6.21 recorded in the previous year. NP margin also dwindled from 13.98 percent in 2018 to 9.77 percent in 2019.2020 was the year when the company recorded impressive margins, never witnessed before. Moreover, despite 6.62 percent dip in net sales, bottomline grew by over 55 percent year-on-year. Suppressed topline was a result of muted offtake of both PVC and Caustic which dipped year-on-year by 15 percent and 27 percent respectively to clock in at 163 KT and 61 KT.The impact of low offtake was partially offset by higher PVC prices and cost control measures implemented during the year. EPCL posted an impressive GP margin of 31 percent in 2020 with gross profit multiplying by 35 percent. Distribution expense declined by 24.83 percent in 2020 due to considerably lower sales promotion expense, lesser salaries and curtailed travelling & conveyance charges incurred during the year.Administrative expense dropped by 3.52 percent in 2020 due to considerable decline in communication, travelling, conveyance and training charges incurred during the year on account of COVID-19. This was partially offset by higher payroll expense incurred during the year as number of employees increased to 563 in 2020. Other expense slumped by 30.77 percent in 2020 due to massive decline in exchange loss.Other expense was completely offset by 26.80 percent higher other income recorded in 2020. This was due to higher income from financial assets at FVTPL and amortized cost. EPCL’s operating profit improved by 52.56 percent in 2020 with OP margin attaining a new high level of 29.51 percent.Finance cost escalated by 22.15 percent in 2020 due to an increase in long-term loan on account of utilization of ILTFF to finance its PVC expansion project. EPCL recorded 55 percent growth in its bottomline which stood at Rs.5730.24 million in 2020. This translated into EPS of Rs.6.28 and NP margin of 16.22 percent.2021 proved to be the most fortunate year for EPCL. Increase in PVC and Caustic volumes coupled with higher PVC prices on account of global supply constraints resulted in 98 percent year-on-year growth in EPCL’s topline which clocked in at Rs.70,021.68 million.PVC volume increased by 28 percent to clock in at 208 KT in 2021. Similarly, caustic soda and caustic flakes also recorded year-on-year growth of 12 percent and 250 percent respectively to clock in at 68 KT and 7 KT. EPCL recorded 119.52 percent improvement in its gross profit with GP margin attaining its highest level of 34.33 percent in 2021.Higher sales volume resulted in 37.92 percent escalation in EPCL’s distribution expense mainly because of increased dealer commission, higher salaries of sales force and elevated travelling, conveyance and training charges incurred during the year.EPCL hired more employees due to completion of its expansionary projects during the year. Workforce stood at 598 employees in 2021. This resulted in higher payroll expense which pushed up the administrative expense by 24.95 percent in 2021. Other expense mounted by 177.21 percent in 2021 due to higher exchange loss and increased provisioning done for WWF and WPPF.Other income ticked up by 12.48 percent in 2021 due to higher income from investment at fair value. EPCL recorded 109.98 percent higher operating profit in 2021 with OP margin jumping up to 31.26 percent.Low discount rate coupled with repayment of loans during the year enabled EPCL to lessen its financial cost by 13.13 percent in 2021. The bottomline of the company grew by 162.83 percent year-on-year in 2021 to clock in at Rs. 15.060.51 million. This translated into EPS of Rs.16.32 and NP margin of 21.51 percent.As against 2021 where the company enjoyed a robust topline and bottomline, 2022 was a rather depressed year for EPCL. During 2022, the company was able to achieve a topline growth of 17.19 percent year-on-year. This was despite low PVC prices due to global economic uncertainty coupled with high volatility in the international energy prices.Topline growth was the result of Pak Rupee depreciation which magnified the value of its export sales. Moreover, PVC sales volume also increased by 11 percent to clock in at 231 KT in 2022. High cost of sales owing to depreciation of Pak Rupee and high fuel and energy (RLNG) charges resulted in 2.73 percent year-on-year drop in the gross profit with GP margin falling down to 28.49 percent.Distribution expense escalated by 44.62 percent in 2022 mainly due to higher dealer commission and sales promotion expense incurred during the year. Administrative expense mounted by 47 percent in 2022 due to inflationary pressure and also because of induction of new employees which took the tally to 601 employees in 2022. Other expense multiplied by 46.12 percent in 2022 due to massive exchange loss incurred during the year on account of Pak Rupee depreciation.Other income grew by 11.62 percent in 2022 due to higher income on bank deposits and income from financial assets at amortized cost. Operating profit slid by 9.61 percent in 2022 with OP margin shrinking to 24.11 percent. Finance cost enlarged by 62.43 percent in 2022 predominantly because of higher discount rate.Net profit slid by 22.39 percent to clock in at Rs.11,689.12 million in 2022 with EPS of Rs.12.39 and NP margin of 14.24 percent.In 2023, EPCL’s topline dipped by 1 percent to clock in at Rs.81,224.45 million. This was due to lower prices and sales volume of both PVC and caustic soda on account of turbulence in the local and global macroeconomic backdrop.Despite thinner topline, cost of sales registered 3.4 percent spike in 2023 on the back of Pak Rupee depreciation and elevated gas prices. This translated into 12.11 percent dip in EPCL’s gross profit in 2023 with GP margin dipping to 25.30 percent.Distribution expense ticked up by 7.19 percent in 2023 as higher salaries and dealer commission was offset by lower sales promotion expense as well as lesser travelling & conveyance charges incurred during the year. Administrative expense mounted by 60.85 percent in 2023 due to higher payroll expense as well as increased cost of purchased services.Lower profit related provisioning and exchange loss culminated into 50.78 percent drop in other expense in 2023 which was almost offset by 15.21 percent higher other income recorded during the year.Higher other income was the result of insurance claim, higher scrap sales, higher profit on bank deposits and income on loan granted to subsidiary companies. Operating profit slid by 9 percent in 2023 with OP margin descending to 22.52 percent.Finance cost magnified by 35.75 percent in 2023 due to higher discount rate and increased utilization of working capital lines. Net profit tapered off by 23.18 percent to clock in at Rs.9230.66 million in 2023. This translated into EPS of Rs.9.45 and NP margin of 11.36 percent.In 2024, EPCL’s topline slid by 6.83 percent year-on-year. There was a slight improvement in PVC demand due to gradual revival in economic activity; however, there was a decline in international PVC prices which put downward pressure on the topline.Overall PVC volumes remained low when compared to the previous year. Caustic soda volumes slightly improved in 2024. Despite topline compression, cost of sales mounted by 13.90 percent in 2024 on the back of higher gas and raw material prices. This resulted in 68 percent contraction in gross profit with GP margin falling down to its lowest level of 8.68 percent in 2024.Distribution expense inched up by 5.46 percent in 2024 due to higher dealer commission, increased cost of purchased services and elevated training, travelling and conveyance charges incurred during the year.Administrative expense soared by 27 percent in 2024 due to exorbitant rise in the cost of purchased services. This was partially offset by lower payroll expense as the company streamlined its workforce from 584 employees in 2023 to 540 employees in 2024.Other expense slumped by 87.95 percent in 2024 as no exchange loss was incurred during the year owing to the stability in the value of local currency. Other income also dwindled by 11.43 percent in 2024 due to considerable decline in the income from investments due to lower cash availability and a drop in discount rate.EPCL registered 71.82 percent year-on-year fall in its operating profit in 2024 with OP margin descending to 6.81 percent. Finance cost escalated by 79.23 percent due to increased short-term and long-term borrowings which was partially offset by lower discount rate. EPCL’s net profit eroded by 93.39 percent to clock in at Rs.610.34 million in 2024 with EPS of Rs.0.45 and NP margin of 0.81 percent.In 2025, EPCL’s topline ticked up by 2.28 percent to clock in at Rs.77,405.67 million. While local demand improved during the year owing to recovery in macroeconomic situation and flood related rehabilitation drives undergoing during the year, domestic PVC prices were significantly reduced in line with declining international prices.Export sales to Afghanistan and the Middle East also shrank during the year due to geopolitical crisis. The demand for caustic soda remained stable during the year. The company also commissioned Rs.11.7 billion Hydrogen peroxide plant during the year.Higher energy cost due to escalating gas prices and downward revision in PVC prices resulted in 19.72 percent deterioration in gross profit in 2025. headline: Monetary policy: the Faustian bargain
summary: Pakistan’s central bank has made external stability the organising principle of monetary policy. But with the rupee appreciating in real terms, reserves barely covering three months of imports, and another energy shock unfolding, the institution that rescued the economy from crisis risks becoming captive to the political economy that created it.The SBP has raised the policy rate by another 50 basis points to 12 percent. Inflation is running above expectations, the Middle East war shows little sign of ending, and global central banks are tightening. Yet Pakistan’s external account remains broadly stable, foreign exchange reserves have reached $21.5 billion, and the rupee continues to hold its ground. For a central bank that has increasingly made external stability the organising principle of monetary policy, there is much to celebrate. Or is there?Central banks generally concern themselves with price stability, employment, output and financial stability, with different mandates assigning different weights to these objectives.In Pakistan, however, the balance of payments has acquired an almost singular importance. And understandably so. Nearly every major macroeconomic crisis in recent memory has culminated in an external financing crunch, reserve depletion, currency depreciation and an eventual return to the IMF. Even inflation has frequently been driven by exchange-rate adjustments rather than domestic demand pressures alone.There is therefore a respectable case for treating external stability as Pakistan’s foremost macroeconomic constraint. But if that is indeed the organising principle, the central bank’s current approach raises some uncomfortable questions. For one, what exactly constitutes external stability? Three months of import cover? A current account deficit contained below one percent of GDP? Or a rupee that has barely moved against the dollar for three years?Consider reserves. At $21.5 billion, SBP’s holdings now cover approximately three months of imports, a milestone the central bank has understandably highlighted.The improvement from the depths of the 2022-23 crisis is substantial. But three months is hardly a particularly reassuring buffer for an economy that has repeatedly found itself scrambling for emergency financing. If external vulnerability is the root of Pakistan’s recurring crises, why should the benchmark for success be the bare minimum conventionally associated with reserve adequacy?For an economy with Pakistan’s history of external financing volatility, six months of import cover would be a more credible ambition. But three months should be a milestone on the way to resilience, not a destination. Especially when a meaningful portion of external support remains dependent on official creditors and rollover arrangements.But the more fundamental contradiction lies elsewhere. How does a central bank that regards external stability as its overriding concern appear so reluctant to allow the exchange rate to perform its most important function?The rupee has traded remarkably close to Rs280 against the dollar since late 2023. Indeed, it has appreciated modestly in recent months. This is extraordinary for a currency that has historically depreciated substantially over time, particularly since domestic inflation persistently exceeds that of major trading partners. Meanwhile, Pakistan’s real effective exchange rate (REER) has climbed to nearly 109, its highest level in eight years.SBP is right to argue that an index reading of 109 does not, by itself, establish that the rupee is overvalued. But the direction of travel is difficult to ignore. With nominal exchange-rate stability and higher relative domestic inflation, the rupee has been appreciating in real terms. That makes imports relatively attractive and places additional pressure on the price competitiveness of domestic production and exports. For an economy supposedly obsessed with external sustainability, it is a peculiar outcome to tolerate.This is especially striking because SBP’s own stated exchange-rate framework describes currency flexibility as the first line of defence against external shocks.The exchange rate is supposed to absorb changing external conditions, allowing reserves and monetary policy to perform their respective functions. Yet the exchange rate appears to have become the one macroeconomic variable that policymakers are least comfortable allowing to adjust.To be clear, the relative stability of the rupee cannot simply be attributed to SBP defending an artificial level through reserve sales. The central bank has been purchasing foreign exchange from the market and rebuilding reserves. That is an important distinction. But it does not settle whether the resulting exchange rate is consistent with medium-term external competitiveness, or whether the broader policy framework has become excessively accommodating of nominal currency stability.This brings monetary policy into the picture. The familiar impossible trinity holds that an economy cannot simultaneously maintain a fixed exchange rate, unrestricted capital mobility and independent monetary policy. If the exchange rate is politically expected to remain stable, monetary policy, domestic demand, external financing and reserve accumulation must collectively accommodate that preference.And that appears increasingly close to Pakistan’s policy equilibrium. Interest rates are adjusted to manage inflation and external pressures, official financing provides additional breathing room, and the currency remains remarkably stable.In the process, the exchange rate’s role as an adjustment mechanism risks being subordinated to its political significance.The irony is that this strategy may itself be undermining the external stability it seeks to preserve. An appreciating real exchange rate can weaken competitiveness and encourage imports, increasing the burden on monetary policy to restrain demand. Meanwhile, the prolonged absence of nominal adjustment creates expectations of continued stability.Businesses, households and the government begin treating the prevailing exchange rate less as a market outcome and more as an economic entitlement. The longer that expectation persists, the more politically costly any subsequent adjustment becomes.The latest monetary policy statement offers little indication that this contradiction is being confronted. Private-sector credit is growing at 14.1 percent, including consumer financing.Non-energy imports are recovering sharply. Headline inflation has reached 10.3 percent and core inflation remains elevated at 8.4 percent. Yet the central bank continues to see economic growth within its earlier projected range and the current account deficit remaining manageable. The policy rate has been raised, but the broader framework still appears designed to preserve recovery without requiring meaningful exchange-rate adjustment.There is a political economy to this. For governments, exchange-rate stability is among the most visible indicators of economic competence. Depreciation is unpopular, immediately inflationary and readily portrayed as evidence of economic mismanagement.Interest-rate adjustments, by comparison, are less visible to the average voter. There is therefore an obvious political preference for keeping the currency stable while using other instruments to manage the consequences.As the political cycle enters its final stretch, that preference is unlikely to weaken. Pressure to sustain growth, protect purchasing power and avoid politically costly adjustments will only increase.The danger is not that another external crisis is inevitable. It is that a framework which repeatedly postpones adjustment can allow vulnerabilities to accumulate beneath apparently reassuring headline indicators. Pakistan has encountered that equilibrium before. It rarely ends well.What makes the present situation particularly unsettling is the leadership at the bank. The incumbents took charge at a time when Pakistan was heading towards one of the worst external crises in its history. Their tenure has since been marked by the restoration of macroeconomic stability, a dramatic reduction in inflation and a rebuilding of foreign exchange reserves. In many respects, Pakistan found its own version of Paul Volcker at precisely the moment it needed one.But the final year of the five-year term presents a different test. It is one thing to make difficult decisions when a crisis is already unfolding and the alternatives have been exhausted. It is quite another to make them when reserves are rising, growth is recovering, the political establishment wants continuity and the next crisis remains beyond the immediate forecast horizon.Perhaps that is the Faustian bargain. The central bank that helped rescue Pakistan from external collapse now finds itself accommodating a political economy in which nominal exchange-rate stability has become synonymous with macroeconomic success. The temptation to preserve the hard-won recovery is understandable. But the cost may be the very flexibility needed to make that recovery sustainable.Pakistan’s version of Volcker may yet be remembered for bringing the economy back from the brink. Whether they are also remembered for helping dismantle the conditions that repeatedly take it there will depend on what happens to the exchange rate before the next committee meeting in seven weeks.

headline: S.S. Oil Mills Limited: performance and outlook
summary: S.S Oil Mills limited (PSX: SSOM) was incorporated in Pakistan as a public limited company in 1990. The principal activity of the company is solvent extraction (edible oil, meal). The company is engaged in the business of extraction, refining, processing and sale of semi-refined washed oil and meal.Pattern of ShareholdingAs of June 30, 2026, SSOM has a total of 5.658 million shares outstanding which are held by 2172 shareholders. Directors, CEO, their spouse and minor children have the major stake of 52.56 percent in the company followed by local general public holding 29.75 percent of the outstanding shares of SSOM.Sikander Commodities (Private) Limited, the parent company of SSOM; accounts for 14.61 percent of its shares.Around 1.68 percent of the company’s shares are held by joint stock companies and 1.09 percent by foreign companies. The remaining ownership is divided among other categories of shareholders.Financial Performance (2021-26)Except for a year-on-year fall in 2023 and 2024, SSOM’s topline followed an upward trajectory over the period under consideration. Its bottomline slid from 2022 to 2024 with net loss registered in the latter year. The company posted net profit in 2025 which further strengthened in 2026. SSOM’s margins portray an indistinct pattern over the period under review.The margins registered significant growth in 2021 followed by a decline in 2022. In 2023, the margins improved and boasted their optimum level only to slide back in 2024. In 2025, the margins recorded phenomenal growth followed by a marginal decline in 2026. The detailed performance review of the period under consideration is given below.SSOM posted a splendid topline growth of 60.38 percent in 2021. This resulted in net sales of Rs.8037.75 million. The sales volume of washed oil and meal & soap showed significant growth of 29 percent and 36 percent respectively. This translated into sales volume of 14,371 M.Tons of washed oil and 66,084 M.Tons of meal and soap in 2021. SSOM operated its plant at 98 percent capacity to produce 88,026 M.tons of product.Cost of sales hiked by 57.61 percent year-on-year in 2021, yet company’s robust sales volume and pricing strategy yielded a stronger GP margin of 7.97 percent in 2021 versus 6.36 percent in 2020. Operating expense mounted by 12.92 percent year-on-year in 2021 which was mainly due higher communication expense, depreciation as well as sales commission.SSOM did massive provisioning for WWF and WPPF in 2021 which inflated its other expense by 415.26 percent to clock in at Rs.35.58 million.Operating profit multiplied by 105.93 percent in 2021 with OP margin jumping up to 6.97 percent from 5.43 percent in 2020. Finance cost which was on the rise in the yesteryears slumped by 38.16 percent in 2021 on account of monetary easing. SSOM incurred lower financing cost despite the fact that its long-term borrowings considerably hiked in 2021 for the purpose of importing Silos and Solar PV plant.SSOM’s net profit marvelously grew by 988.43 percent in 2021 to clock in at Rs.311.57 million. This translated into an EPS of Rs.55.06 and NP margin of 3.88 percent in 2021 versus EPS of Rs.5.06 and NP margin of 0.57 percent registered in the previous year.The uphill journey of SSOM’s topline continued in 2022 with 31.41 percent improvement in net sales which clocked in at Rs.10,652.35 million. The sales volume of washed oil improved by 19.42 percent to clock in at 17,162 M.Tons in 2022. Conversely, the sales volume of meal and soap was recorded at 57,784 in 2022, down 12.7 percent. Capacity utilization of plant dropped to 86 percent in 2022 translating into production volume of 77.815 M. Tons.Steep depreciation in the value of Pak Rupee and global commodity super cycle on account of Russia-Ukraine crisis inflated the company’s cost of sales by 33 percent in 2022. Hiked cost couldn’t be completely passed on to the consumers due to their squeezed purchasing power.As a consequence GP margin plunged to 6.86 percent in 2022. Operating expense drastically surged by 35.21 percent in 2022 due to higher utility charges, vehicle running expense and freight & forwarding charges – all pointing towards elevated prices of POL products and electricity.Operating profit could only rise by 13.23 percent in 2022 with OP margin eroding to 6 percent. Finance cost elevated by 81.18 percent year-on-year in 2022 on account of monetary tightening and increased borrowings. This drove the net profit down by 29.41 percent year-on-year in 2022 to clock in at Rs.219.93 million with an EPS of Rs.38.87 and NP margin of 2.10 percent.Defying the uphill journey of the preceding years, SSOM’s net sales registered 41 percent year-on-year slump to clock in at Rs.6230.79 million in 2023. This was on account of a huge plunge of 67 percent and 64 percent in the sales volume of washed oil and meal and soap respectively. This translated into sales volume of 5,628 M.Tons of washed soap and 20,656 M.tons of meal & soap in 2023. This was the consequence of a ban imposed on the import of GMO seeds as well as general import restrictions imposed by the SBP in the wake of diminishing foreign exchange reserves of the country.The company operated its plant at 31 percent capacity which was the lowest since 2018. This culminated into a production volume of 27,687 M.Tons in 2023. The company increased its prices in accordance with the cost hike. This resulted in an improved GP margin of 9.28 percent – the highest since 2018.SSOM also kept a check on its operating expense in 2023 which slid by 20.14 percent due to a significant drop in freight & forwarding and sales commission on account of thinner sales volume. Bottomline plummeted by 38.92 percent year-on-year to clock in at Rs.134.34 million. This translated into an EPS of Rs.23.74 and NP margin of 2.16 percent.In 2024, SSOM’s net sales further deteriorated by 27.52 percent to clock in at Rs.4516.35 million. This was the result of 37.75 percent year-on-year decline in the sales volume of meal & soap which clocked in at 12,859 M tons. This was due to decline in the company’s cash & bank balances during the year, indicating liquidity constraints. Operating profit plummeted by 64.23 percent in 2024, resulting in OP margin of 4.12 percent.Finance cost escalated by 67 percent in 2024 due to monetary tightening and a considerable spike in short-term borrowings. SSOM posted net loss of Rs.122.99 million in 2024. This translated into loss per share of Rs.21.74 in 2024.SSOM’s registered a staggering 73.35 percent year-on-year improvement in its sales in 2025 which clocked in at Rs.7828.87 million. Operating expense registered 53.38 percent spike in 2025 mainly on the back of elevated freight & forwarding charges incurred during the year due to heightened sales volume. Other income posted 40.28 percent growth in 2025 due to higher profit on bank deposits.While discount rate was reduced during the year, improved liquidity due to higher sales resulted in higher mark-up income in 2025. SSOM posted 153.34 percent stronger operating profit in 2025 with OP margin picking up to 6 percent.Finance cost slid by 36.46 percent in 2025 due to monetary easing and reduced external borrowings. The company posted net profit of Rs.250.63 million in 2025, resulting in an EPS of Rs.44.29 and NP margin of 3.20 percent.SSOM registered a robust topline growth of 74.79 percent in 2026. This resulted in net sales of Rs.13,684.35 million. Sales volume of washed oil was recorded at 15,236 M tons in 2026, up 123.60 percent year-on-year.Meal & soap segment posted sales volume of 55,909 M tons in 2026, up 81.35 percent year-on-year. This was due to increase in the availability of GMO seeds in the international market coupled with the stability of Pak Rupee and improvement of overall economic indicators in the home market.Gross profit increased by 62.61 percent in 2026, however, GP margin slightly fell to 6.89 percent. Operating expense mounted by 19.76 percent in 2026 due to enhancement in the company’s operations and sales volume. This particularly pushed up the payroll expense and commission expense in 2026. SSOM also enhanced its workforce from 135 employees in 2025 to 149 employees in 2026. Other income strengthened by 108 percent in 2026 due to higher income on bank deposits.However, it was offset by 79.81 percent higher other expense recorded in 2026 which was the result of increased provisioning done for WWF and WPPF. SSOM posted 70.27 percent improvement in its operating profit in 2026 with OP margin falling to 5.87 percent.Lower average borrowings rates translated into 34.95 percent lesser finance cost in 2026 despite increased short-term borrowings. This resulted in 60.16 percent higher net profit to the tune of Rs.401.427 million in 2026. This culminated into EPS of Rs.70.94 and NP margin of 2.93 percent in 2026.Future OutlookWith the lifting of import restrictions, the company may be in a better position to import soybean and continue its production to meet the growing demand.However, with the authorities’ inclination towards making the country GMO free, the company’s cost of production will rise as non-GMO seed varieties are relatively costly. To mitigate this risk, the management has entered into forward purchase agreements to fix the procurement pricing and ensure raw material availability.

headline: Tarar says referendum constitutional way to ascertain public opinion on new provinces
summary: Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar on Tuesday said a referendum was a constitutional and legal mechanism to ascertain public opinion, stressing that no political party should have reservations about seeking the people’s views on administrative reforms and the creation of new provinces.Responding to a statement byPakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, the minister said good governance, institutional reforms and public welfare were shared objectives of all political parties, adding that people wanted effective and accountable governance.He said the ongoing debate on governance and provincial arrangements should not be suppressed, as citizens had the right to express their views on matters concerning their welfare and the country’s administrative structure.“The real question is what problem there is in approaching the people on this matter,” he said, adding that the decision about what people wanted should rest with them rather than political leaders.Tarar said the country had remained under successive governments for decades, making it difficult for political stakeholders to dissociate themselves from the weaknesses of the existing system. He added that using politics as a shield against accountability was unacceptable to both the law and the public.Questioning criticism of the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), he said reforms in the institution had also been introduced by those now holding it responsible for its shortcomings.The minister also termed it contradictory for political parties to enjoy government positions and privileges while simultaneously projecting themselves as opposition.Referring to the debate on the creation of new provinces, he said the issue should be considered constructively rather than turned into a political controversy.“If the people of Pakistan and Sindh want more provinces, they should be created; otherwise, they should not,” he said, maintaining that public representatives derived their authority from the people and must respect their aspirations.He said the past misuse of referendums could not justify depriving citizens of their constitutional right to express their opinion. No individual, he added, could impose a personal agenda on the people of Sindh, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan without first ascertaining their views.Tarar urged coalition partners to sit together and reach a decision in the national interest, based on public opinion.He said the debate should continue both inside and outside parliament, with all stakeholders given an opportunity to participate.The minister also called for stronger protection of journalists’ rights, saying the federal government was working in this regard and would continue its efforts.He urged the Sindh government to take notice of reported incidents of journalists’ exploitation and fulfil its responsibility towards their protection.He stressed that the ongoing discussion should not create an impression of restricting public opinion, adding that the people’s interests and aspirations must remain central to the debate.

headline: Every creative mind deserves a chance to shine
summary: Every generation has ideas, dreams, and abilities that deserve recognition. Some young people have a natural talent for writing and poetry, others are interested in art, communication, technology, research and innovation, while many have fresh perspectives on how society can become better.Pakistan is blessed with an energetic and talented young population, full of creative minds and individuals who have the potential to make meaningful contributions to society. Yet, despite their abilities and ambitions, countless young people struggle to find the right direction, guidance, and encouragement to turn their potential into reality.One of the biggest challenges facing Pakistan’s youth is not a lack of talent but the difficulty of getting that talent recognised. Every year, thousands of students graduate from colleges and universities with dreams of building successful careers, but many find themselves facing unemployment, intense competition, and uncertainty about their future.For those interested in creative fields, the challenges can be even greater. Writers, poets, artists, researchers, and aspiring media professionals often struggle to gain recognition in an environment where conventional career choices are generally given greater importance.The situation is particularly difficult for talented young people who belong to middle- and lower-income families. Many have creative ideas and ambitions but cannot afford professional training, specialised courses or the resources required to develop their skills. Some have the ability to write, communicate, create or innovate but lack access to experienced individuals who could guide them. Others live in smaller towns and less developed areas, where exposure to professional communities and creative activities remains limited. As a result, considerable talent goes unnoticed, while many promising individuals eventually abandon their ambitions because of financial and social pressures.Pakistan’s education system also faces the challenge of adequately recognising creativity and independent thinking. Academic qualifications and examination results remain important, but they do not always reflect an individual’s imagination, communication skills, leadership qualities or ability to solve problems. Many students are encouraged to follow conventional career paths, while their interests in literature, journalism, art, filmmaking, digital media, and other creative disciplines receive comparatively little attention. There is a need to create an environment in which young people are encouraged not only to acquire degrees but also to explore their abilities, question established ideas and develop confidence in their own potential.Another major concern is the growing gap between education and the professional world. Young graduates often find that the knowledge acquired in classrooms does not adequately prepare them for practical challenges. They need to understand workplace expectations, develop communication skills, and gain practical experience. Unfortunately, mentorship and professional networking are not equally available to everyone. A student studying at a well-established institution in a major city may have exposure to professional networks that remain out of reach for an equally talented student in a smaller town.The rapid growth of digital media and technology has created new possibilities for the younger generation, but it has also brought its own challenges. Social media provides an opportunity to showcase talent, share ideas, and reach wider audiences.However, visibility does not always translate into professional growth, recognition or financial stability. Young content creators, writers, artists, and digital entrepreneurs often struggle to establish credibility, develop sustainable careers, and distinguish meaningful creative work from the overwhelming volume of online content. They need guidance to use these platforms constructively and turn their interests into practical achievements.A platform that genuinely seeks to encourage creativity must first create an atmosphere in which young people feel confident enough to express themselves without fear of criticism or rejection.It is equally important to recognise talent beyond major urban centres and privileged communities. Pakistan has creative and intelligent young people in every province, city, town, and village. A talented student in a remote area may have the same imagination, determination, and ability as someone studying at a prestigious university in Karachi, Lahore or Islamabad. The difference often lies in exposure, financial circumstances and family support rather than individual potential. Young people should not be judged by their backgrounds or the institutions they attend.Experienced journalists, writers, communication specialists, and other professionals can play an important role in helping address these challenges. Their knowledge and practical experience can help emerging talent understand professional standards, improve their skills, and explore different career paths.Mentorship programmes, workshops, interactive sessions, and opportunities for young people to present their work can provide valuable learning experiences. headline: Former England striker Rooney says he contemplated suicide during playing career
summary: Former England and Manchester United striker Wayne Rooney contemplated suicide during his playing career, he said in a podcast episode released on Tuesday.One of the country’s most decorated players, Rooney spent the early years of his career battling mental health issues and alcoholism, he told the “Life at the Midpoint” podcast.“It took until my mid-20s, until I hit rock bottom (before I started feeling comfortable with myself),” Rooney, 41, said.“I’d go home and lock myself in the house for two days, and just drink. Probably at the best part of my career playing-wise.”“I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.”Rooney said it pushed his marriage to breaking point but wife Coleen was key in his recovery. Even so, he said he did not feel alcohol abuse affected his performances on the pitch.Rooney labels Man United players ‘selfish’ after Fernandes criticism“I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else (I) really struggled with it.”Although Rooney eventually attended therapy sessions, he said the culture around mental health and masculinity in football prevented him from seeking help earlier.“You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,” he said.“Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that.”Rooney retired from playing football in 2021 and has since worked as a manager, most recently for Plymouth Argyle in 2024.His managerial career has been shared with punditry, and Rooney is currently appearing on British reality TV show “I’m a Celebrity Get Me Out of Here”.

Inside inDrive’s driver safety training across Pakistan
summary: Cultivating trust behind the steering wheel requires a lot more than implementing the latest technology. It also requires a shared commitment to road etiquette, personal accountability, and continuous learning. Building this culture from the ground up, inDrive regularly conducts comprehensive nationwide safety workshops that bring drivers together for practical, face to face training sessions across Pakistan.The comprehensive training curriculum goes beyond basic transit logistics, focusing heavily on foundational road safety.Drivers review essential traffic laws, speed limit adherence, pre-trip vehicle inspection protocols, and defensive driving techniques designed to manage adverse weather conditions and prevent accidents.Alongside road rules, sessions also focus on professional conduct, boundary management, and effective de-escalation strategies to calmly handle aggressive, unpredictable, or intoxicated passengers.Additionally, a dedicated passenger safety module instructs participants on maintaining professional etiquette, identifying safe boarding and drop-off zones, strictly following agreed routes, and providing specialized assistance for elderly, disabled, or vulnerable commuters.Drivers are also guided on how to respond appropriately during unexpected roadside breakdowns, accidents, or security incidents.Beyond behavioral coaching, the training provides an in-depth walkthrough of inDrive’s embedded digital safety architecture. Drivers explore pre-ride tools, which display passenger ratings and exact destination details before trip acceptance.To protect personal privacy, in-app calls and chats eliminate the need to share personal phone numbers, while AI-powered moderation filters out aggressive language and automatically issues 30-day bans to non-compliant accounts.The program also covers active in-trip safeguards, including proactive trip monitoring that detects prolonged stops to check on driver well-being.Drivers learn to use encrypted in-app audio recording as an effective conflict deterrent, emergency SOS integration for instant one-tap police or ambulance access, and the ability to designate up to 5 trusted contacts whom support teams can reach out to in critical situations.These sessions are designed to create financial security by reviewing inDrive’s comprehensive accident and health insurance coverage in Pakistan, provided in partnership with Waada.Renewed annually, this policy protects active rides by covering accidental death, total disability, immediate medical expenses, and hospital cash benefits.By combining rigorous behavioral workshops, advanced digital guardrails, and robust financial protection, inDrive continues to build a high-trust mobility community that empowers drivers and protects commuters across Pakistan.

Iran attacks US military radar system in Bahrain with drones
summary: DUBAI: Iran fired drones at a US military radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday as tensions in the Gulf remained high, despite talks between Tehran and Oman on safeguarding maritime corridors in the Strait of Hormuz after nearly nine months of war.Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards said the radar system that it attacked was at the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain, the Arab Gulf state that is home to the US Fifth Fleet.Bahrain said it had intercepted the attack after sending an air raid alert and telling citizens to take shelter. There were no reports of casualties or damage.Bahrain had also intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks on Sunday, during which Tehran said it had targeted a US radar system at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base after what it said were hostile US actions.The war has ground to a stalemate, with US President Donald Trumpsaying he might hold off from attacking Iran if the US does not face what he described as provocations from Tehran or the Houthi group in Yemen.Araghchi warns states against aiding attacks on IranBut Trump has said he will maintain a US naval blockade on Iran in response to Tehran’s continued disruption of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global energy supplies and other trade.Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi was on Tuesday visiting Oman, which lies on the opposite side of the Strait of Hormuz to Iran and has mediated in the conflict that began with US and Israeli attacks on Iran on February 28.Araqchi discussed safeguarding maritime corridors and ensuring the smooth flow of global shipping and trade with Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi, the Omani foreign ministry said. The two also talked about revitalising channels for dialogue and negotiation to prevent escalation.“These efforts aim to expand areas of mutual understanding among the concerned parties and prevent the widening of the crisis and its repercussions,” the ministry said in a statement.Oman, Iran foreign ministers discuss safeguarding maritime corridorsAttacks on tankers increaseLast week, Iran attacked ship navigation systems on the Omani island of Didamar, which lies in the strait. Gulf exporters have been increasingly using workarounds to raise oil flows via Hormuz.Attacks on tankers have increased in the waterway, which carried about one-fifth of global energy supplies before the war and is a sticking point in negotiations on ending the conflict.Oman and Iran have previously held on-and-off talks about controlling traffic in the strait, most recently in August. Before the ​war, shipping passed freely ⁠through the strait, which sits in the territorial waters of both countries but is generally regarded as an international waterway.The disruption to shipping has threatened oil supplies and caused global economic problems.Iran’s Araqchi says he discussed regional peace, security with Field Marshal Asim MunirThe war also continues to spill over into other parts of the Middle East as Iran puts pressure on Washington through its Houthi allies, who have carried out attacks on Saudi Arabia and seized areas along the Yemeni coast on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, hoping to squeeze Gulf oil producers.Crackdown in BahrainTuesday’s attack on Bahrain followed the sentencing there of 64 people, mostly Shi’ite clerics, to life in prison on charges of colluding with Iran to undermine the state.Bahrain, a Shi’ite-majority country ruled by a Sunni Muslim family, has launched a crackdown on Shi’ite clerics since Tehran began attacking it this year following the US-Israeli strikes, but it has long been anxious about Iranian influence.Among those sentenced to life imprisonment was Sheikh Isa Qassim, who is widely regarded as the spiritual ​leader of Bahrain’s Shi’ite community and has lived ⁠in Iran since 2018, according to the Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy.Iran’s foreign ministry condemned the court’s ruling on Tuesday and said the accusations were baseless. Tehran has long denied interference in Bahrain’s internal affairs.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned Iranian strikes in Bahrain during a call on Monday with Bahrain’s foreign minister.

headline: IPL career over, Dhoni unveiled as Chennai team mentor
summary: NEW DELHI: Mahendra Singh Dhoni will take over as team mentor at the Chennai Super Kings, the Indian Premier League (IPL) franchise said on Tuesday, confirming the retirement of arguably the most adored player in the history of the league.The 45-year-old, who captained Chennai to a record five IPL titles and two Champions League Twenty20 crowns, quit international cricket in 2020.“There is no CSK without MS Dhoni,” Super Kings owner N Srinivasan said in a statement.“In 2008, I insisted that Dhoni should be part of CSK…It turns out that’s the best decision I took. Not because of all his achievements for the franchise, but for the kind of human he is.”“Dhoni will always be a part of our identity. This will always be his home.”Dhoni, who hails from Ranchi, enjoys huge popularity in the southern Indian city of Chennai where crowds throng stadium just to get a glimpse of their “Thala”, the Tamil word for leader.Mumbai trade captain Pandya to Punjab in exchange for Arshdeep in IPLRuns stopped flowing from his blade in recent years but legions of his fans still filled the stands to watch Dhoni batting lower down the order.Even that was not possible this year, however, and Dhoni sat out the entire season with a calf strain, which effectively signalled the end of his career.Dhoni has been the face of the franchise since joining them in 2008 and played two seasons with Rising Pune Super Giant only when Chennai were handed a two-year suspension following a corruption scandal.“While we will miss seeing him in yellow on the field, we are glad that he will keep guiding our players,” Chennai managing director KS Viswanathan said.“The bond will continue to grow and shape this team for years to come.”Nicknamed “Captain Cool” for his astute leadership and unflappable temperament, Dhoni led India to World Cup titles in the 20 and 50-over one-day formats

headline: Drought risk feared in four Sindh districts as NDMA issues high alert
summary: The National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) has issued a high alert for several districts of Sindh over the risk of severe drought conditions.According to the NEOC, parts of Umerkot, Tharparkar, Mirpurkhas and Sujawal districts are facing a high risk of severe drought. The situation is being continuously monitored by the centre.Some areas of Balochistan’s Chagai and Washuk districts are also experiencing drought conditions, the NEOC said.It attributed the emerging situation to below-normal rainfall, prolonged dry spells, rising temperatures and changes in the monsoon rainfall pattern.Temperatures in the affected areas of Sindh are being recorded 1 to 3 degrees Celsius above normal, further aggravating the situation.Water shortages have severely affected agricultural activities and crop production in the affected areas, raising concerns about food insecurity, according to the NEOC.The NDMA has directed relevant departments to ensure the effective use of available water resources and take precautionary measures to protect affected farming and rural communities.It has also advised residents to follow instructions issued by relevant departments and take necessary steps to protect their crops and livestock.

headline: Grand Theft Auto VI heads to launch amid feverish anticipation
summary: Vacation days have been booked. Millions of copies of the game have been preordered and preloaded. One gamer even asked a spouse to promise, in writing, not to interrupt.Take-Two Interactive’s Rockstar Games’ action-adventure video game series “Grand Theft Auto” returns on Thursday with its first new title in 13 years and gamers are rearranging their lives to participate in a shared cultural moment rarely seen in this era of fragmented audiences. “Grand Theft Auto VI” is the latest installment in a franchise that turned American excess into satire, outsold some of Hollywood’s biggest blockbusters and drew the fury of lawmakers with its graphic violence.“Everyone’s talking about it, all my friends at work and just talking online … it really feels like a whole societal coming together in a way,” said Owen Donahue, a 23-year-old from Los Angeles who works in the TV industry.“Grand Theft Auto” began in 1997 with a top-down, heavily pixelated game that involved stealing cars and carrying out jobs for crime syndicates. With each installment, the graphics and storyline became more sophisticated. GTA V, released in 2013 by Take-Two Interactive’s Rockstar Games and set in an alternative Los Angeles called Los Santos, was one of the best-selling video games of all time.But that was 13 years ago. The wait for the next one has been so long that it became a running joke in gaming circles, with many players only children at the last launch. Every sliver of the title’s footage has been devoured, from its first trailer that has drawn more than 300 million YouTube views since its release nearly three years ago, to an August gameplay preview that briefly crashed Netflix.Take-Two sticks to annual bookings outlook, says on track for ‘GTA VI’ November launchPaid time-off requests for launch day have been running about 13% higher than a normal November day, according to data from BambooHR, which runs a platform that helps small- and medium-sized businesses track schedules. Further employees are likely to call in sick on Thursday, it says. A BambooHR survey of 1,500 US adults found about one-third of Gen Z workers plan to take the day off.“This is at a scale and size that we have not seen in other entertainment launches,” said BambooHR CEO Brad Rencher.Singaporean gamer Julian Tay said in a social media post that he had drawn up a five-point “GTA VI Gaming Agreement” for his spouse, covering the first 10 days after launch and stipulating when missions could be interrupted and when hugs, kisses and errands were allowed.Some companies are embracing the fervor. Logitech, which makes gaming hardware, is giving employees an extra day off called “Game Day.”“I’m going to enter flow state and what that means is basically I’m going to complete the entire game and not get off of it until I complete it,” said Brayden Whaley, a 23-year-old content creator from Los Angeles.Welcome to Vice CityThe game takes players to the neon-lit streets of Vice City, a fictional version of Miami. The game features two playable characters — partners-in-crime Lucia and Jason, a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde who get drawn into a wide-ranging conspiracy after a heist goes wrong. Lucia is the first fleshed-out playable female character in the series, addressing a common complaint from female gamers at a time when the gaming audience is increasingly skewing older and less male. Women make up nearly half of US players, according to the Entertainment Software Association.In the US, the game sells for $79.99, with a $99.99 Ultimate Edition that adds extra cars, weapons, and outfits. With a production budget of an estimated $1 billion or more, “Grand Theft Auto VI” is one of the most expensive games ever made.That makes the launch a major test not just for Rockstar Games and owner Take-Two Interactive Software, but for a gaming market hit by slowing sales and weaker demand for aging consoles.Early sales have been strong, but glitches or a game that falls short of expectations could prove costly. Still, by many metrics it is already a hit.“With an estimated 10 million pre-orders at an average price close to $100, GTA VI clears $1 billion in consumer spending the moment it goes live, two days faster than its predecessor and before anyone has played it,” said Joost van Dreunen, games professor at NYU’s Stern School of Business. Market research firm Newzoo estimates at least $3.25 billion in first-week sales across the Sony PlayStation 5 and Microsoft Xbox Series X and S gaming consoles.“At a cultural level, I feel GTA VI already succeeded,” said Bob De Schutter, professor of art and design at Northeastern University. “The Netflix preview went straight to (the top of) its rankings, pushing movies and TV shows aside. No game has ever accomplished something like that.”
